name: NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp
doc:
An **Arnoldi decomposition** of `(A, b)` of size `q`: a matrix `Q` whose columns form a graded
orthonormal Krylov basis. The compression `H = Qᵀ A Q` is `ArnoldiDecomp.H`; for symmetric `A`
the same object is a `LanczosDecomp` with `T = H`. Exists iff `q ≤ krylovGrade A b`
(`arnoldiDecomp`, `IsGradedKrylovBasis.le_krylovGrade`); unique up to column signs
(`ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.3 (Alg. 6.1, Prop. 6.4);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33.

the last unit vector of `ℝ^q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5, eq. (6.7);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2.

  A * (D.restrict ⋯).Q =

**The Arnoldi relation** (outer-product form): `A Q_q = Q_q H_q + q_{q+1} h̲ᵀ` where
`h̲ = (h_{q+1,1}, …, h_{q+1,q})` is the last row of `H̲_q`. No hypothesis beyond the
decomposition of size `q + 1`; by the Hessenberg structure `h̲ = h_{q+1,q} e_q`
(`mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_smul`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5, eq. (6.7);
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33, eq. (33.13).

  (hcond : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = ∫ (ω : Ω), cfac ω * Y ω ∂μ) (hYbound : ∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ ≤ B)

  ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ ≤ cmax * B

doc:
Abstract assembly of Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:GN` (Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1).
* `X = ‖A − Â‖_F²`, `Y = ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²` (the range-finder error),
  `cfac ω = 1 + q(ω)/(s − q(ω) − 1)` with `q = rank(AΩ)` the (random) number of columns of `Q`.
* `hcond` encodes `lem:completion` after the tower property (conditioning on `Ω`, using
  independence of `Ψ` and `Ω`): `E X = E[(1 + q/(s−q−1)) Y]`.
* `hc` is the deterministic bound `q ≤ t` and monotonicity of `q ↦ q/(s−q−1)`
  (`completion_factor_mono`).
* `hYbound` is the range-finder theorem (`thm:RSVD`).
Atlas `gn-expected-error`.

Hypotheses: `hc` (`lem:completion`'s factor with `q = rank(AΩ) ≤ t`), `hcond`
(`lem:completion` + tower property), `hstruct` (`prop:hmt-struct` for
`Y = ‖(I−QQᵀ)A‖_F²`), `hZ` (`lem:moments` + `lem:invmom`, as in the proof of `thm:RSVD`).
The hypothesis `hk` is not used by the arithmetic; it is kept for fidelity.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (uses `rsvd-expected-error`).

name: NLAlib.Assembly.integral_le_sqrt_integral_sq
doc:
Jensen's inequality in the form used throughout Chen–Persson: for a nonnegative
square-integrable random variable `Y`, `E Y ≤ √(E Y²)`. Proved from
`0 ≤ Var Y = E Y² − (E Y)²`. Helper for atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (Frobenius-norm,
unsquared form of HMT 2011, Thm 10.5).

signature:
NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hanson_wright_inequality.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {n : ℕ} {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} {X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} {K C t : ℝ}
  (hK : 0 < K) (hC : 0 < C) (hC_domain : 4 * Real.exp 1 ≤ C) (hC_diag_quad : 8 * Real.exp 1 ^ 3 ≤ C)
  (hC_offdiag_domain : 16 * Real.exp 1 ≤ C ^ 2) (hC_offdiag_quad : 64 * Real.exp 1 ^ 2 ≤ C)
  (hF : 0 < NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A)
  (hOp : 0 < NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A) (h_indep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hX_subG : ∀ (i : Fin n), ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF (X i) ⟨K ^ 2, ⋯⟩ μ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  (μ {ω | t ≤ |NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.centeredQuadraticForm μ A X ω|}).toReal ≤
    2 *
      Real.exp
        (-(1 / (4 * C)) *
          min (t ^ 2 / (K ^ 4 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A ^ 2))
            (t / (K ^ 2 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicOperatorNorm A)))

doc:
Hanson-Wright tail bound with the MGF certificate proved from sub-Gaussian coordinates.

This theorem does not take `HasHansonWrightMGF` as a hypothesis.  Instead it proves
that certificate from independence and coordinate sub-Gaussian MGF bounds, then
optimizes the resulting Chernoff bound.

  (hX_bound : ∀ (i : Fin n), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, |X i ω| ≤ K)
  (hC_bound :
    2 * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.entrywiseL1Norm A ^ 2 ≤
      C * NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.deterministicFrobeniusNorm A ^ 2) :
  NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.HasHansonWrightMGF μ A X K C
name: NLAlib.HansonWrightProof.hasHansonWrightMGF_of_bounded
doc:
A proved Hanson-Wright MGF certificate for bounded coordinates.

If each coordinate satisfies `|Xᵢ| ≤ K` almost surely, then the quadratic form lies
in the interval `[-K²‖A‖₁, K²‖A‖₁]`.  The centered quadratic form is therefore
bounded by `2K²‖A‖₁`; the local bounded MGF lemma above gives a quadratic CGF
estimate.  The explicit side condition compares this bounded-coordinate constant
with the Frobenius-scale constant used by the Hanson-Wright tail statement.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} (E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)) (x : n → ℝ) :
  Prop
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser
doc:
`x` minimises the objective `E` over the affine space `x₀ + S`: `x − x₀ ∈ S` and
`E x ≤ E (x₀ + y)` for every `y ∈ S`. Minimising Krylov methods (CG, GMRES, MINRES, LSQR,
sketched GMRES) are instances with `S` a Krylov space. Non-uniqueness is harmless: theorems
quantify over every minimiser. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §5.1 (optimality of projection
methods); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.apply_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}
  {x' : n → ℝ} (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ S x) (hx' : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ S x') : E x = E x'
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.apply_eq
doc:
Two minimisers over the same affine space have the same value.
Source: KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser E x₀ (NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) x)
  (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  E x ≤ E (xs + ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs))
name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_aeval
doc:
**K1, error form.** If `x` minimises any objective `E` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` and
`A x⋆ = c`, then `E x ≤ E (x⋆ + p(A)(x₀ − x⋆))` for every residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`). No hypothesis on `A` or `E`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Thm 6.29 (proof); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (proof); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (consumer: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound`).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_aeval_residual
doc:
**K1, residual form.** If `x` minimises an objective of the residual,
`y ↦ F (c − A y)`, over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then `F (c − A x) ≤ F (p(A) r₀)` for every
residual polynomial `p`. No solution `x⋆` is needed (GMRES on singular or inconsistent
systems). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32 (proof); KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.3.
Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (consumer: `gmres-def`).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

name: NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_of_le
doc:
**Monotonicity.** A minimiser over a larger space is at least as good:
`S ≤ S'` gives `E x' ≤ E x`. With `S = K_q`, `S' = K_{q+1}` this is monotonicity of a
minimising Krylov method in the iteration count. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6
(GMRES residuals are nonincreasing).

signature:
NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser.le_of_sub_mem.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} {E : (n → ℝ) → ℝ} {x₀ x : n → ℝ} {S : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)}

doc:
A minimiser beats every point of the affine space: `z − x₀ ∈ S → E x ≤ E z`.

signature:

name: NLAlib.IsCGIterate
doc:
`x` is a `q`-th conjugate-gradient iterate for `A x = c` from `x₀`: `x − x₀` lies in
`K_q(A, c − A x₀)` and `x` minimises `cgObjective A c` over `x₀ + K_q(A, c − A x₀)`, i.e.
`IsAffineMinimiser (cgObjective A c) x₀ (krylovSpace A (c − A x₀) q) x`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2 (variational form). Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
Deviation: a predicate rather than the output of the Hestenes–Stiefel recurrence.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate
doc:
`x` is a `q`-th CGLS (equivalently, in exact arithmetic, LSQR) iterate for
`min ‖b − A x‖` from `x₀`: it minimises `‖b − Ay‖²` over `x₀ + K_q(AᵀA, Aᵀ(b − Ax₀))`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3 (CGNR); Paige–Saunders (1982) [`ps82`]. Deviation: a
predicate, not the Golub–Kahan recurrence.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ)
  (x : n → ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate
doc:
`x` is a GMRES iterate: `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` (`r₀ = c − A x₀`) and `x` minimises
`‖c − A y‖²` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`. MINRES is this predicate for symmetric `A`.
Source: Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §2; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5;
KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.3.
atlas: gmres-def

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_of_eigenvalues_mem_Icc.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)

doc:
**MINRES, definite case (Chebyshev rate).** If `A` is symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`, then `‖r_q‖ ≤ 2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q ‖r₀‖` (squared form).
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Liesen–Strakoš (2013) [`ls13`], §5.6.
atlas: minres-bound (partial)

signature:

  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} {V W : Matrix n n ℝ} {d : n → ℝ} (hVW : V * W = 1)
  (hAd : A = V * Matrix.diagonal d * W) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)

  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤
    (NLAlib.specNorm V * NLAlib.specNorm W * M) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)

Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.4.

complex diagonalisation, which is not available over `ℝ`).

NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_sq_mul_of_isHermitian.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) {M : ℝ}
  (hM : ∀ (i : n), |Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p| ≤ M) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤ M ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.dotProduct_le_sq_mul_of_isHermitian
doc:
**MINRES spectral bound.** For symmetric `A` and every residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, the GMRES (= MINRES) residual
satisfies `‖r_q‖² ≤ M² ‖r₀‖²`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Paige–Saunders
(1975) [`ps75`].
Deviation: no invertibility of `A` and no solution `x⋆` needed (the bound is on residuals).
atlas: minres-bound (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.eq_of_isUnit
doc:
**The GMRES iterate is unique for invertible `A`.** Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval
doc:
**Polynomial form of the residual**: `c − A x = p(A) r₀` for a residual polynomial `p`
(`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6; Trefethen–Bau (1997)
[`tb97`], Lect. 35.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.isLeast_dotProduct_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  IsLeast
    {v |
      ∃ p,
        p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧
          Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧
            v = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)}
    ((c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x))
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.isLeast_dotProduct_aeval
doc:
**`‖r_q‖² = min_{p ∈ 𝒫_q⁰} ‖p(A) r₀‖²`**: the squared GMRES residual is the least value of
`‖p(A) r₀‖²` over residual polynomials. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6;
Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35 (GMRES as a polynomial approximation problem).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_aeval.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  (c - A.mulVec x) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) ≤
    ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_aeval
doc:
**GMRES beats every residual polynomial**: `‖r_q‖² ≤ ‖p(A) r₀‖²` for every `p` with
`deg p ≤ q` and `p(0) = 1`. No hypothesis on `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.32
(proof); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 35.2 (proof).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.le_of_le
doc:
**GMRES residuals are nonincreasing**: for `q ≤ q'`, `‖r_{q'}‖² ≤ ‖r_q‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.6; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq
doc:
**The GMRES residual is unique**: two GMRES iterates for the same data have the same
residual `c − A x`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1 (the residual is the orthogonal
projection of `r₀` onto `(A K_q)^⟂`).
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : IsUnit A) (hx : NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x)
  (hq : NLAlib.krylovGrade A (c - A.mulVec x₀) ≤ q) : c - A.mulVec x = 0
name: NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate.sub_mulVec_eq_zero_of_krylovGrade_le
doc:
**Finite termination.** For invertible `A`, a GMRES iterate with `q` at least the grade
`ν = krylovGrade A r₀` solves the system: `c − A x = 0`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`],
Prop 6.10 (no breakdown before the solution) and §6.5.6; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §3.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ}
  (Q : Matrix n (Fin q) ℝ) : Prop
name: NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis
doc:
`Q` is a **graded orthonormal Krylov basis** of `(A, b)`: its columns are orthonormal and for
every `i < q` the first `i + 1` columns span `K_{i+1}(A, b)`. Equivalently (`of_mem`), the
columns are orthonormal and `q_i ∈ K_{i+1}(A, b)`. Such a basis exists iff `q ≤ krylovGrade A b`
and is unique up to the signs of its columns (`ArnoldiDecomp.exists_sign`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3 and §6.6; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.5.
atlas: graded-krylov-basis-def

signature:
NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis.casesOn.{u, u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}

  (t : NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis A b Q)
  (mk :
    (orth : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) →
      (nested :
          ∀ (i : Fin q),
            Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun j => Q.col (Fin.castLE ⋯ j)) = NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (↑i + 1)) →
        motive ⋯) :
  motive t

**Hessenberg structure**: for a graded basis, `(Qᵀ A Q)_ij = 0` whenever `i > j + 1`, for
every `A`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.5; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 33.

`(Qᵀ A Q)_{j+1, j} ≠ 0`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.6 (breakdown at step `j`
iff `K_{j+1}` is invariant). Atlas: `graded-krylov-basis-def`.

Any real SVD computes the same Moore–Penrose inverse, independently of the
choice of singular vectors. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs : n → ℝ) : (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error `E‖x_k - xs‖²` after `k` randomized Kaczmarz steps started at `x`,
rows drawn i.i.d. with probabilities `prob A`. Defined by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x - xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ i, prob A i * expErr k (step A b x i)`.
See `expErr_eq_sum_paths` for the path-sum form. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
atlas: kaczmarz-def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k =
    ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_eq_sum_paths
doc:
`expErr` is the expectation over i.i.d. row sequences: the sum over all `ω : Fin k → m` of
`(∏ j, prob A (ω j)) * ‖run A b k ω x - xs‖²`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz converges linearly in expectation.**
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
If `A *ᵥ xs = b` and `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`, then after `k` steps with rows drawn
i.i.d. with probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ - xs‖²`.
Deviations from the printed statement: SV09 take `A` of full column rank and `σ = ‖A⁻¹‖⁻¹`
(rate `1 - κ(A)⁻²`); here `σ` is any constant satisfying `hσ` (the sharp choice is
`σ_min(A)`, atlas `courant-fischer`), and no rank or nonzero-row assumption is needed.
atlas: randomized-kaczmarz

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xh : n → ℝ) (σ : ℝ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xh x k ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xh) ⬝ᵥ (x - xh) +
      (∑ j ∈ Finset.range k, (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ j) *
        ((b - A.mulVec xh) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xh) / NLAlib.frobSq A)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz on inconsistent systems.** If `σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²` for all `v`, then for
any reference point `xh` and `e = b − A xh`, with `ρ = 1 − σ²/‖A‖_F²`,
`E‖x_k − xh‖² ≤ ρ^k ‖x₀ − xh‖² + (∑_{j<k} ρ^j) ‖e‖²/‖A‖_F²`.
Source: Needell (2010) [`needell10`], Thm 2.1 (stated for norms, with `xh` the least-squares
solution); Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`], eq. (5) (squared form).
Atlas: `kaczmarz-inconsistent`; uses `randomized-kaczmarz`.
Deviation: any reference point `xh` (no least-squares or consistency assumption); the geometric
sum is kept exact.
atlas: kaczmarz-inconsistent

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add_div_sq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xh : n → ℝ) {σ : ℝ} (hσ0 : 0 < σ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)
  (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xh x k ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xh) ⬝ᵥ (x - xh) + (b - A.mulVec xh) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xh) / σ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_add_div_sq
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz on inconsistent systems, horizon form.** If `σ > 0` and
`σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²` for all `v`, then for any `xh`,
`E‖x_k − xh‖² ≤ (1 − σ²/‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x₀ − xh‖² + ‖b − A xh‖²/σ²`.
Source: Needell (2010) [`needell10`], Thm 2.1 (squared form, `R = ‖A‖_F²/σ²`);
Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`], Thm 2. Atlas: `kaczmarz-inconsistent`.
atlas: kaczmarz-inconsistent

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_of_sub_mem_range.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ v ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range, σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ)
  (hx : x - xs ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b xs x k ≤ (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_le_of_sub_mem_range
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz on rank-deficient consistent systems.** If `A xs = b`, the initial
error `x − xs` lies in the row space `range Aᵀ`, and `σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²` for every `v` in the row
space, then `E‖x_k − xs‖² ≤ (1 − σ²/‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x − xs‖²`.
Source: Strohmer–Vershynin (2009) [`sv09`], Thm 2 in the form of Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`],
Thm 2 (`σ = σ_min⁺(A)`, the smallest nonzero singular value).
Atlas: `kaczmarz-rank-deficient`; uses `randomized-kaczmarz`.
atlas: kaczmarz-rank-deficient

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_succ.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero_le_moorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (hb : ∃ y, A.mulVec y = b) (k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr A b ((NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A).mulVec b) 0 k ≤
    (1 - (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A))⁻¹ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k *

name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expErr_zero_le_moorePenroseInverse
doc:
**Randomized Kaczmarz converges to the least-norm solution.** For a consistent system
(`b ∈ range A`) started at `x₀ = 0`,
`E‖x_k − A⁺b‖² ≤ (1 − ‖A⁺‖⁻²/‖A‖_F²)^k ‖A⁺b‖²`, with no rank assumption.
Source: Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`], Thm 2 (`b ∈ range A`, `x₀ = 0`);
Needell–Tropp (2014), §1. Atlas: `kaczmarz-rank-deficient`; uses `pseudoinverse`.
atlas: kaczmarz-rank-deficient

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (hA : A ≠ 0) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_eq
doc:
One-step expected error identity:
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - ‖A (x - xs)‖² / ‖A‖_F²` for `A ≠ 0`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le
doc:
One-step contraction of randomized Kaczmarz: if `σ² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖A v‖²` for all `v`
(`σ` a lower bound on the smallest singular value, atlas `courant-fischer`), then
`∑ i, prob A i * ‖step A b x i - xs‖² ≤ (1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²) ‖x - xs‖²`.
No hypothesis on `A` (for `A = 0` the left side is `0` and the rate is `1`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le_add.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xh x : n → ℝ) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :
  ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i * (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xh) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xh) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) * (x - xh) ⬝ᵥ (x - xh) + (b - A.mulVec xh) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec xh) / NLAlib.frobSq A
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.expected_sqErr_step_le_add
doc:
One-step bound for inconsistent systems: if `σ²‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²` for all `v`, then for any `xh`
`∑ᵢ pᵢ ‖step A b x i − xh‖² ≤ (1 − σ²/‖A‖_F²) ‖x − xh‖² + ‖b − A xh‖²/‖A‖_F²`.
Source: Needell (2010) [`needell10`], proof of Thm 2.1. Atlas: `kaczmarz-inconsistent`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.inv_specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_sq_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) {v : n → ℝ} (hv : v ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range) :
  (NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A))⁻¹ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.inv_specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_sq_mul_le
doc:
The Moore–Penrose lower bound on the row space: for `v ∈ range Aᵀ`,
`‖A⁺‖⁻² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖²`. Source: Zouzias–Freris (2013) [`zf13`], §2 (`σ_min⁺ = ‖A⁺‖⁻¹`).
Atlas: `kaczmarz-rank-deficient` (helper).

signature: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (i : m) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob
doc:
Row-selection probability `‖A i‖² / ‖A‖_F²` of randomized Kaczmarz.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
atlas: kaczmarz-def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (i : m) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob_nonneg
doc: Selection probabilities are nonnegative. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.rate_nonneg.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Nonempty n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (σ : ℝ) (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) :

The contraction factor is nonnegative when `n` is nonempty: `σ² ≤ ‖A‖_F²`.
Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  (Fin k → m) → (n → ℝ) → n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run
doc:
The iterate after applying the steps with rows `ω 0, ω 1, …, ω (k-1)` in that order,
starting from `x`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
atlas: kaczmarz-def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x✝ : ℕ)
  (x✝¹ : Fin x✝ → m) (x✝² : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b x✝ x✝¹ x✝² =
    match (motive := (x : ℕ) → (Fin x → m) → (n → ℝ) → n → ℝ) x✝, x✝¹, x✝² with
    | 0, x, x_1 => x_1
    | k.succ, ω, x => NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k (Fin.tail ω) (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x (ω 0))
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run.eq_def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (i : m) :
  (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)) ^ 2 / A i ⬝ᵥ A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step
doc:
Pythagoras for one Kaczmarz step (the step is an orthogonal projection onto a hyperplane
containing `xs`): `‖step A b x i - xs‖² = ‖x - xs‖² - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs))² / ‖A i‖²`.
Holds for every row; for a zero row both sides equal `‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step_eq_add.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xh x : n → ℝ) (i : m) :
  (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xh) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xh) =
    (x - xh) ⬝ᵥ (x - xh) - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xh)) ^ 2 / A i ⬝ᵥ A i + (b i - A i ⬝ᵥ xh) ^ 2 / A i ⬝ᵥ A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sqErr_step_eq_add
doc:
One Kaczmarz step from an arbitrary reference point `xh` (no consistency assumed): with
`e = b − A xh`,
`‖step A b x i − xh‖² = ‖x − xh‖² − (Aᵢ ⬝ (x − xh))²/‖Aᵢ‖² + eᵢ²/‖Aᵢ‖²`.
Source: Needell (2010) [`needell10`], proof of Thm 2.1. Atlas: `kaczmarz-inconsistent`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (x : n → ℝ)
  (i : m) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step
doc:
One Kaczmarz step on row `i`: the orthogonal projection of `x` onto the hyperplane
`{y | A i ⬝ᵥ y = b i}`. For a zero row the step is the identity (real division by zero is `0`).
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Algorithm (eq. (2)); atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.
atlas: kaczmarz-def

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_mem_range.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (hx : x - xs ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range)
  (i : m) : NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs ∈ A.transpose.mulVecLin.range
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_mem_range
doc:
Kaczmarz steps keep the error in the row space: if `A xs = b` and `x − xs ∈ range Aᵀ`, then
`step A b x i − xs ∈ range Aᵀ`. Atlas: `kaczmarz-rank-deficient` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_solution.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ)
  (xs x : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (i : m) :
  NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step A b x i - xs = x - xs - (A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) / A i ⬝ᵥ A i) • A i
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.step_sub_solution
doc:
Error recursion of one Kaczmarz step when `A *ᵥ xs = b`:
`step A b x i - xs = (x - xs) - ((A i ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)) / ‖A i‖²) • A i`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, proof of Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_paths_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (σ : ℝ)
  (hσ : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σ ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v) (x : n → ℝ) (k : ℕ) :
  ∑ ω,
      (∏ j, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A (ω j)) *
        (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.Kaczmarz.run A b k ω x - xs) ≤
    (1 - σ ^ 2 / NLAlib.frobSq A) ^ k * (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_paths_le
doc:
Path-sum form of SV09 Thm 2: the weighted average over all row sequences of length `k` of
the squared error is at most `(1 - σ² / ‖A‖_F²)^k ‖x - xs‖²`.
Strohmer–Vershynin 2009, Thm 2; atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature:
NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_prob.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (hA : A ≠ 0) : ∑ i, NLAlib.Kaczmarz.prob A i = 1
name: NLAlib.Kaczmarz.sum_prob
doc: The selection probabilities sum to one when `A ≠ 0`. Atlas `randomized-kaczmarz`.

signature: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Type u_1
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp
doc:
A **Lanczos decomposition**: an Arnoldi decomposition, used for symmetric `A` (then
`T = Qᵀ A Q` is a Jacobi matrix, `LanczosDecomp.T`). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`],
Ch. 4.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin q) ℝ
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T
doc:
The Jacobi matrix `T_q = Q_qᵀ A Q_q` of a Lanczos decomposition (the Hessenberg matrix `H_q`
under its Lanczos name). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T_apply_eq_zero_of_one_lt_dist
doc:
**For symmetric `A`, `T_q` is tridiagonal**: `t_ij = 0` whenever `|i − j| > 1`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence, graded-krylov-basis-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T_eq_jacobiMatrix.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsSymm) : D.T = NLAlib.jacobiMatrix D.alpha D.beta q
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T_eq_jacobiMatrix
doc:
For symmetric `A`, `T_q` is the Jacobi matrix of its recurrence coefficients:
`T_q = jacobiMatrix α β q`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2.
Atlas: `jacobi-matrix-identities`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.X_mul_poly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsSymm) {j : ℕ} (hj : j + 1 < q) :
  Polynomial.X * D.poly j =
    Polynomial.C (D.beta j) * D.poly (j - 1) + Polynomial.C (D.alpha j) * D.poly j +
      Polynomial.C (D.beta (j + 1)) * D.poly (j + 1)
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.X_mul_poly
doc:
**Three-term recurrence of the Lanczos polynomials**: for symmetric `A` and `j + 1 < q`,
`X p_j = β_j p_{j−1} + α_j p_j + β_{j+1} p_{j+1}`, so the Jacobi matrix `T` holds the recurrence
coefficients of the orthonormal polynomials of `μ_b`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`],
Thm 2.1 and Thm 4.2.
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.alpha.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.alpha
doc:
The Lanczos diagonal coefficient `α_j = t_jj = q_jᵀ A q_j` (`0` for `j ≥ q`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta
doc:
The Lanczos off-diagonal coefficient `β_j = t_{j,j−1} = q_jᵀ A q_{j−1}` (`β_0 = 0`, and `0`
for `j ≥ q`). Indexing: `A q_j = β_j q_{j−1} + α_j q_j + β_{j+1} q_{j+1}` (0-based columns).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1 (there `η_j`). Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta_arnoldiDecomp_pos.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (h : q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b) {j : ℕ} (h0 : 0 < j) (hj : j < q) :
  0 < NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta (NLAlib.arnoldiDecomp A b q h) j
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta_arnoldiDecomp_pos
doc:
The canonical (Gram–Schmidt) decomposition has positive `β_j` for `0 < j < q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Alg. 4.1 (`η_j = ‖v_j‖ > 0`).
Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta_ne_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) {j : ℕ} (h0 : 0 < j) (hj : j < q) : D.beta j ≠ 0
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.beta_ne_zero
doc:
The Lanczos off-diagonal coefficients do not vanish below the grade: `β_j ≠ 0` for
`0 < j < q`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2 (no breakdown before the grade).
Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence`.

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.cfc_T_apply_zero_zero
doc:
**Golub–Welsch**: `e₁ᵀ f(T_q) e₁ = ∑ᵢ f(θᵢ) (uᵢ)₁²` with `(θᵢ, uᵢ)` the eigenpairs of
`T_q`: the Gauss rule has the eigenvalues of `T_q` as nodes and the squared first components
of its eigenvectors as weights. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 6 (Golub–Welsch; label to
verify).
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.charpoly_T_monic.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) : D.T.charpoly.Monic ∧ D.T.charpoly.natDegree = q
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.charpoly_T_monic
doc: `charpoly T_q` is monic of degree `q`. Atlas: `lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.charpoly_restrict_T_mul_poly_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsSymm) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) :
  (NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯)).charpoly * D.poly 0 =
    Polynomial.C (∏ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 j, D.beta k) * D.poly j
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.charpoly_restrict_T_mul_poly_zero
doc:
**`det(x I − T_j)` is proportional to the Lanczos polynomial `p_j`**:
`χ_j p_0 = β_1 ⋯ β_j p_j` with `χ_j = charpoly T_j` (`p_0 = ±1/‖b‖` is a constant; for
`‖b‖ = 1` and the canonical signs this is `det(x I − T_j) = β_1 ⋯ β_j p_j(x)`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3 and Thm 4.2 (labels to verify).
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.col_dotProduct_vec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (i : Fin q) (k : ℕ) : D.Q.col i ⬝ᵥ D.vec k = if ↑i = k then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.col_dotProduct_vec
doc: `q_i ⬝ q_k = δ_ik` in the `ℕ`-indexed form. Atlas: `lanczos-recurrence`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.degree_poly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}
  (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) {j : ℕ} (hj : j < q) : (D.poly j).degree = ↑j
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.degree_poly
doc: `deg p_j = j` for `j < q`. Atlas: `lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.degree_poly_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ}
  {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (j : ℕ) : (D.poly j).degree ≤ ↑j
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.degree_poly_le
doc: The Lanczos polynomials have degree at most `j` (exactly `j` for `j < q`).

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Gauss–Lanczos quadrature through the Jacobi matrix**: for symmetric `A`, `q ≥ 1` and
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = ‖b‖² (p(T_q))₁₁`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6
and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`], Thm 2.1. Deviation: the degree bound is
`p.degree < 2 * q` (no `natDegree`, no truncated subtraction).
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
**Gauss quadrature through the Jacobi matrix**: for symmetric `A`, `q ≥ 1` and
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = ‖b‖² ∑ᵢ p(θᵢ) (uᵢ)₁²` with nodes `θᵢ` the eigenvalues of `T_q` and
weights the squared first eigenvector components. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`],
Thm 6.6; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`], Thm 2.1.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature, jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_cfc_T_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hq : 0 < q) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
  D.Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ (cfc f D.T).mulVec (D.Q.transpose.mulVec b) =
    b ⬝ᵥ b * ∑ i, f (⋯.eigenvalues i) * (⋯.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⟨0, hq⟩ ^ 2
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.dotProduct_cfc_T_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
**The Lanczos quadrature value is a Gauss rule**: `(Q_qᵀ b)ᵀ f(T_q) (Q_qᵀ b) =
‖b‖² ∑ᵢ f(θᵢ) (uᵢ)₁²` for every `f`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1;
Ubaru–Chen–Saad (2017) [`ucs17`], §3.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial), lanczos-gauss-quadrature (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_restrict_T.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {q' : ℕ} (h : q' ≤ q)
  (i : Fin (Fintype.card (Fin q'))) :
  ⋯.eigenvalues₀ ⟨↑i + (Fintype.card (Fin q) - Fintype.card (Fin q')), ⋯⟩ ≤ ⋯.eigenvalues₀ i
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_restrict_T
doc:
**Cauchy interlacing, lower half**: `θ_{i + (q − q')}(T_q) ≤ θ_i(T_{q'})` for `q' ≤ q`;
with `q' = q − 1` and the upper half, the eigenvalues of `T_{q−1}` interlace those of `T_q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3 (label to verify); Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`],
Thm 4.3.17.
Deviation: non-strict.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.eigenvalues₀_restrict_T_le
doc:
**Cauchy interlacing, upper half**: the eigenvalues of `T_{q'}` (`q' ≤ q`, a leading
principal submatrix of `T_q`) satisfy `θ_i(T_{q'}) ≤ θ_i(T_q)` (eigenvalues in non-increasing
order). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3 (interlacing; label to verify);
Horn–Johnson (2013) [`hj13`], Thm 4.3.17. Deviation: non-strict.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.exists_col_eq_aeval
doc:
Each Lanczos vector is a polynomial of exact degree `j` in `A` applied to `b`:
`q_j = p_j(A) b` with `deg p_j = j`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2 (§4.1).
Atlas: `lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials`.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_eval_charpoly_mul_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {r : Polynomial ℝ}
  (hr : r.degree < ↑q) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x D.T.charpoly * Polynomial.eval x r ∂NLAlib.spectralMeasure hA b = 0
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_eval_charpoly_mul_eq_zero
doc:
**`det(x I − T_q)` is the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree `q`**: for symmetric `A`,
`χ_q = charpoly T_q` (monic of degree `q`, `charpoly_T_monic`, `natDegree_charpoly_T`) is
orthogonal in `μ_b` to every polynomial of degree `< q`. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010)
[`gm10`], Thm 4.2 and §3.1 (`p_q` and `det(λI − J_q)` are proportional).
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_poly_mul_poly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i j : ℕ} (hi : i < q) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), Polynomial.eval x (D.poly i) * Polynomial.eval x (D.poly j) ∂NLAlib.spectralMeasure hA b =
    if i = j then 1 else 0
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.integral_poly_mul_poly
doc:
**The Lanczos polynomials are orthonormal for the spectral measure**:
`∫ p_i p_j dμ_b = δ_ij` for `i < q` (and any `j`; `p_j = 0` for `j ≥ q`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2 and §2.1; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.5.
atlas: lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.inv_smul_one_sub_T_apply_zero_zero
doc:
**The resolvent entry is the Jacobi continued fraction**: for symmetric `A`, `q ≥ 1` and
`x` above the spectrum of `A`, `e₁ᵀ (x I − T_q)⁻¹ e₁ = 1/(x − α₀ − β₁²/(x − α₁ − ⋯ −
β_{q−1}²/(x − α_{q−1})))`, the `q`-th convergent of the continued fraction of the Stieltjes
transform `∫ dμ_b(t)/(x − t)` (for `‖b‖ = 1`). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3
(continued fractions; label to verify) and Thm 4.2. Deviation: real `x` above the spectrum
(so every trailing block is nonsingular); complex `x` off the real axis is not covered.
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.mulVec_vec_eq
doc:
**The Lanczos three-term recurrence** (column form): for symmetric `A` and `j + 1 < q`,
`A q_j = β_j q_{j−1} + α_j q_j + β_{j+1} q_{j+1}` (with `β_0 = 0`). Together with
`ArnoldiDecomp.mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_smul` this is `A Q_q = Q_q T_q + β_q q_{q+1} e_qᵀ`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 36,
eq. (36.3).
atlas: lanczos-recurrence, arnoldi-relation (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_beta_smul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b (q + 1)) (hq : 0 < q) :
  A * (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯).Q =
    (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯).Q * NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.T (NLAlib.ArnoldiDecomp.restrict D ⋯) +
      D.beta q • Matrix.vecMulVec (D.vec q) (Pi.single ⟨q - 1, ⋯⟩ 1)
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.mul_restrict_Q_eq_add_beta_smul
doc:
**The Lanczos relation** `A Q_q = Q_q T_q + β_q q_{q+1} e_qᵀ` (for `q ≥ 1`), with
`β_q = t_{q,q−1}` and `q_{q+1}` the last column of a decomposition of size `q + 1`; together with
`T_apply_eq_zero_of_one_lt_dist` (`T_q` symmetric tridiagonal for symmetric `A`) and
`ArnoldiDecomp.hasOrthonormalCols`, `ArnoldiDecomp.range_Q` this is the Lanczos
tridiagonalisation. Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 4.2; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021)
[`ctu21`], §2.
atlas: lanczos-recurrence

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.poly.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}

doc:
The **Lanczos polynomial** `p_j` (indexed by `ℕ`, `0` for `j ≥ q`): the polynomial of degree
`j` with `q_j = p_j(A) b` (unique below the grade, `eq_zero_of_aeval_mulVec_eq_zero`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], §4.1 and Ch. 2. Atlas: `lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials`.

name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.posDef_smul_one_sub_T
doc: For `x` above the spectrum of `A`, `x I − T_q` is positive definite.

signature:
NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.sub_mul_sum_eval_poly_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {b : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (D : NLAlib.LanczosDecomp A b q) (hA : A.IsSymm) {m : ℕ} (hm0 : 0 < m) (hm : m < q) (x y : ℝ) :
  (x - y) * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range m, Polynomial.eval x (D.poly j) * Polynomial.eval y (D.poly j) =
    D.beta m *
      (Polynomial.eval x (D.poly m) * Polynomial.eval y (D.poly (m - 1)) -
        Polynomial.eval x (D.poly (m - 1)) * Polynomial.eval y (D.poly m))
name: NLAlib.LanczosDecomp.sub_mul_sum_eval_poly_mul
doc:
**Christoffel–Darboux identity** for the Lanczos polynomials: for symmetric `A` and
`1 ≤ m < q`, `(x − y) ∑_{j<m} p_j(x) p_j(y) = β_m (p_m(x) p_{m−1}(y) − p_{m−1}(x) p_m(y))`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 2 (Christoffel–Darboux formula; label to
verify).
atlas: jacobi-matrix-identities (partial)

doc:

Hermitian `A`, `H` of every size with spectra in `I`. Tropp 2015, Def. 8.4.6. Atlas:

signature:
NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn.matrixFunction_conjTranspose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty κ] (I : Set ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (hf : NLAlib.OperatorConvexOn I f) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hAI : spectrum ℝ A ⊆ I) (K : Matrix ι κ ℂ)
  (hK : K.conjTranspose * K = 1) :

doc:
Operator Jensen inequality for an isometry: if `f` is operator convex on `I` and `Kᴴ K = 1`, then
`f (Kᴴ A K) ≼ Kᴴ f(A) K`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 8.5.2 (single-isometry form). Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from the
Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

NLAlib.SketchProject.dotProduct_mulVec_le_dotProduct_self.{u_5, u_6} {p : Type u_5} {q : Type u_6} [Fintype p]
  [Fintype q] (M : Matrix p q ℝ) (d : q → ℝ) : d ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse M * M).mulVec d ≤ d ⬝ᵥ d

The projector is a contraction in the quadratic-form sense: `dᵀ (M⁺M) d ≤ dᵀd`.
Atlas: `sketch-and-project` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} {J : Type u_4} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) (xs : n → ℝ) :
  (n → ℝ) → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr
doc:
Expected squared error after `k` sketch-and-project steps from `x`, sketches `S j` drawn
i.i.d. with probabilities `p j`, by first-step recursion:
`expErr 0 x = ‖x − xs‖²`, `expErr (k+1) x = ∑ⱼ pⱼ expErr k (step A b (S j) x)`.
Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr.eq_def.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} {J : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ)
  (xs x✝ : n → ℝ) (x✝¹ : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr A b p S xs x✝ x✝¹ =
    match x✝, x✝¹ with
    | x, 0 => (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs)
    | x, k.succ => ∑ j, p j * NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr A b p S xs (NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b (S j) x) k
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr.eq_def
NLAlib.SketchProject.expErr_le
doc:
**Sketch-and-project converges linearly in expectation.** Let `A xs = b`, `pⱼ ≥ 0`,
`∑ pⱼ = 1`, and `λ ‖v‖² ≤ vᵀ W v` for all `v`, with `W = ∑ⱼ pⱼ (SⱼᵀA)⁺(SⱼᵀA)`. Then after `k`
steps with i.i.d. sketches, `E‖x_k − xs‖² ≤ (1 − λ)^k ‖x₀ − xs‖²`.
Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015) [`gr15`], Thm 4.6 (`B = I`; the sharp `λ` is
`λ_min⁺(W)`). Atlas: `sketch-and-project`; uses `pseudoinverse`. Deviation: finite sketch
distribution; expectation modelled by first-step recursion.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} {J : Type u_4}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (p : J → ℝ) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) : Matrix n n ℝ
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector
doc:
The expected projector `W = ∑ⱼ pⱼ (SⱼᵀA)⁺(SⱼᵀA)`. Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015) [`gr15`],
eq. (4.1) (`E[Z]` with `B = I`). Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.expected_sqErr_step_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3}
  {J : Type u_4} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype s] [Fintype J] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (p : J → ℝ)
  (hp1 : ∑ j, p j = 1) (S : J → Matrix m s ℝ) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b) (x : n → ℝ) :
  ∑ j, p j * (NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b (S j) x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b (S j) x - xs) =
    (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (x - xs) - (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ (NLAlib.SketchProject.expectedProjector A p S).mulVec (x - xs)
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.expected_sqErr_step_eq
doc:
One-step expected error identity: for `A xs = b` and `∑ pⱼ = 1`,
`∑ⱼ pⱼ ‖step A b (S j) x − xs‖² = ‖x − xs‖² − (x − xs)ᵀ W (x − xs)`.
Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015) [`gr15`], proof of Thm 4.6. Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.step.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [Fintype s] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (S : Matrix m s ℝ) (x : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.SketchProject.step
doc:
One sketch-and-project step with sketch `S`: the Euclidean projection of `x` onto
`{y | Sᵀ A y = Sᵀ b}`, written `x − (SᵀA)⁺ Sᵀ (A x − b)`. Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015)
[`gr15`], eq. (2.2)–(2.3) with `B = I`. Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.
atlas: sketch-and-project

signature:
NLAlib.SketchProject.step_sub_solution.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {s : Type u_3} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [Fintype s] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (b : m → ℝ) (S : Matrix m s ℝ) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = b)

  NLAlib.SketchProject.step A b S x - xs =

Error recursion: if `A xs = b` then `step A b S x − xs = (I − Z)(x − xs)` with the
projector `Z = (SᵀA)⁺(SᵀA)`. Source: Gower–Richtárik (2015) [`gr15`], eq. (4.3).
Atlas: `sketch-and-project`.

The derivative of `T_q` is bounded by `q²` on `[-1, 1]`: `|x| ≤ 1 → |T_q'(x)| ≤ q²`.

`chebyshev-second-kind`.
atlas: chebyshev-second-kind

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : |x| < 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q * M / √(1 - x ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Bernstein's inequality** for algebraic polynomials. If `p` has degree at most `q` and
`|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q M / √(1 − x²)` for `|x| < 1`.

Source: Bernstein (1912); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7; Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
Proof (algebraic form of the trigonometric argument): with `a = x = cos θ₀`, `b = √(1 − x²)`, the
odd part of `θ ↦ p(cos(θ₀ + θ))` is `sin θ · r(cos θ)` for a polynomial `r` of degree `< q` (built
from Hasse derivatives of `p`), `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, and `r(1) = −b p'(x)`; Schur's
inequality `abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` at `y = 1` gives
`b |p'(x)| ≤ q M`.
atlas: bernstein-polynomial-inequality

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval y p| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.derivative p)| ≤ ↑q ^ 2 * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality** (the first Markov inequality, sharp constant). If `p` has
degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|p'(x)| ≤ q² M` for all `x ∈ [−1, 1]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), Thm 2.24 / §2.7;
Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
Proof: Bernstein's inequality `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le` gives
`√(1 − y²) |p'(y)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`, and Schur's inequality
`abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le` applied to `p'` (degree `< q`) gives
`|p'(x)| ≤ q · q M`. The equality case (`p = ±M T_q`, `x = ±1`) is not formalised.
atlas: markov-brothers

name: NLAlib.abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Markov brothers' inequality on an interval.** If `p` has degree at most `q` and `|p| ≤ M` on
`[a, b]` (`a < b`), then `|p'(x)| ≤ 2 q² / (b − a) · M` for all `x ∈ [a, b]`.

Source: A. A. Markov (1889); Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (affine
rescaling of `abs_eval_derivative_le_sq_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`). Atlas: `markov-brothers`.
atlas: markov-brothers

signature:

`[−1, 1]`.
Source: Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le_one {q : ℕ} {P : Polynomial ℝ} {x : ℝ} (hP : P.degree ≤ ↑q)

doc:
Chebyshev's extremal growth bound: if `P` has degree at most `q` and `|P| ≤ 1` on `[−1, 1]`,
then `|P(x)| ≤ |T_q(x)|` for every `|x| ≥ 1`.
Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (1990), Thm 2.20 (case `k = 0`); Mathlib
`Polynomial.Chebyshev.eval_iterate_derivative_le_of_forall_abs_le_one` covers `x ≥ 1`;
Atlas: `chebyshev-extremal`.
atlas: chebyshev-extremal

signature:

  (hb : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ M) (hx : 1 ≤ |x|) :
  |Polynomial.eval x P| ≤ M * |Polynomial.eval x (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)|
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_abs_eval_T_real_of_forall_abs_le
doc:
Scaled form of Chebyshev's extremal growth bound: if `P` has degree at most `q` and
`|P| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then `|P(x)| ≤ M |T_q(x)|` for every `|x| ≥ 1`. No sign condition on `M`
(for `M ≤ 0` the hypothesis forces `P = 0`).
Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (1990), Thm 2.20 (case `k = 0`);
Atlas: `chebyshev-extremal`.
atlas: chebyshev-extremal

signature:
NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le {q : ℕ} {r : Polynomial ℝ} {M x : ℝ} (hq : 0 < q)
  (hr : r.degree < ↑q) (hM : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, √(1 - y ^ 2) * |Polynomial.eval y r| ≤ M) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1) :
  |Polynomial.eval x r| ≤ ↑q * M
name: NLAlib.abs_eval_le_mul_of_forall_sqrt_one_sub_sq_mul_abs_eval_le
doc:
**Schur's inequality.** If `r` has degree `< q` and `√(1 − y²) |r(y)| ≤ M` on `[−1, 1]`, then
`|r(x)| ≤ q M` on `[−1, 1]`.

Source: Rivlin, *Chebyshev Polynomials* (2nd ed., 1990), §2.7 (Schur's lemma); Cheney,
*Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Proof: for `|x| ≤ cos(π/(2q))` directly from
`√(1 − x²) ≥ sin(π/(2q)) ≥ 1/q`; for `x ≥ cos(π/(2q))` by Lagrange interpolation at the zeros
`ξ_k` of `T_q`, where all partial nodal products are nonnegative and the weights satisfy
`|r(ξ_k)| / |T_q'(ξ_k)| ≤ M/q`, so `|r(x)| ≤ (M/q) T_q'(x) ≤ q M`; the case `x ≤ −cos(π/(2q))` by
reflection. Atlas: auxiliary for `markov-brothers` and `bernstein-polynomial-inequality`.
atlas: schur-polynomial-inequality

signature: NLAlib.bernsteinTail (dimension : ℕ) (v L t : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.bernsteinTail
doc:
The matrix Bernstein tail `d · exp (-(t²/2)/(v + L t/3))`, defined piecewise in the degenerate
case `v + L t/3 = 0`. Tropp 2015, Thm 6.1.1. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`.
atlas: matrix-bernstein

signature:
NLAlib.bernstein_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L θ : ℝ) (hL : 0 < L)
  (hθ : 0 < θ) (hθL : θ < 3 / L) (hMeas : Measurable X) (hHerm : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X ω).IsHermitian)
  (hL2 : MeasureTheory.MemLp X 2 μ) (hMean : ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hBound : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (X ω) ≤ L) :
  NLAlib.LoewnerLE (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ)
      (NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ^ 2 ∂μ)) ∧
    NLAlib.LoewnerLE (NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp (θ • X ω) ∂μ))
      ((θ ^ 2 / 2 / (1 - θ * L / 3)) • ∫ (ω : Ω), X ω ^ 2 ∂μ)
name: NLAlib.bernstein_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a centered Hermitian random matrix with `λmax X ≤ L` and `0 < θ < 3/L`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼
matrixExp (c • 𝔼 X²)` and `matrixLog 𝔼 matrixExp (θ • X) ≼ c • 𝔼 X²`, where `c = (θ²/2)/(1 -
θL/3)`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 6.6.2. Atlas: `matrix-bernstein`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.

signature:
NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (K : ι → ℝ)
  (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i)) (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (hK : ∀ (i : ι), 0 < K i)
  (hmean : ∀ (i : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|X i ω| / K i)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (B : ℝ) (hB : 0 < B)
  (hKB : ∀ (i : ι), K i ≤ B) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  μ {ω | t ≤ |∑ i, X i ω|} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-(1 / 64) * min (t ^ 2 / ∑ i, K i ^ 2) (t / B)))
name: NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two
doc:
**Scalar Bernstein inequality from genuine `ψ₁` exponential bounds.** For mutually
independent centered real coordinates with positive scales satisfying
`E exp(|Xᵢ|/Kᵢ)≤2`, and any positive `B` dominating those scales,
`P(|ΣXᵢ|≥t)≤2exp(-min(t²/ΣKᵢ²,t/B)/64)` for `t≥0`.
The family may be empty; all moment and exponential-integrability conditions are derived.
Vershynin 2018, Theorem 2.8.4; atlas `bernstein-scalar`.
atlas: bernstein-scalar

signature:
NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two_uniform.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (K : ℝ)
  (hX : ∀ (i : ι), Measurable (X i)) (hindep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ) (hK : 0 < K)
  (hmean : ∀ (i : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X i ω ∂μ = 0)
  (hpsi : ∀ (i : ι), ∫⁻ (ω : Ω), ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (|X i ω| / K)) ∂μ ≤ 2) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
  μ {ω | t ≤ |∑ i, X i ω|} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-(1 / 64) * min (t ^ 2 / (↑(Fintype.card ι) * K ^ 2)) (t / K)))
name: NLAlib.bernstein_sum_of_lintegral_exp_abs_le_two_uniform
doc:
Uniform-scale scalar Bernstein bound from genuine `ψ₁` exponential moments:
`P(|ΣXᵢ|≥t)≤2exp(-min(t²/(N K²),t/K)/64)` for independent centered coordinates.
The bound also covers the empty family. Vershynin 2018, Theorem 2.8.4;
atlas `bernstein-scalar` (common-scale corollary).
atlas: bernstein-scalar

signature: NLAlib.bestRankFrobSq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (k : ℕ) (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : ℝ

The actual rank-constrained optimal squared Frobenius error, as an

signature:
NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Submodule ℝ (n → ℝ)
name: NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace
doc:
The block Krylov subspace `K_q(A, Ω) = span {(A^i Ω) e_j : i < q, j ∈ s}`, the range of
`[Ω, AΩ, …, A^(q−1)Ω]`. Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Alg. 2; Saad (2011) [`saad11`],
§6.3.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_eq_iSup.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) (q : ℕ) : NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q = ⨆ j, NLAlib.krylovSpace A (Ω.col j) q
name: NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_eq_iSup
doc:
The block Krylov space is the sum of the single-vector Krylov spaces of the columns:
`K_q(A, Ω) = ∑_j K_q(A, Ω e_j)`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_mono.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
  (Ω : Matrix n s ℝ) {q q' : ℕ} (h : q ≤ q') : NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q ≤ NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace A Ω q'
name: NLAlib.blockKrylovSpace_mono
doc:
Block Krylov spaces are nested: `q ≤ q' → K_q(A, Ω) ⊆ K_{q'}(A, Ω)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3.
atlas: block-krylov-subspace

A real matrix with orthonormal columns has at most as many columns as rows.

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_diagonal_real.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (f : ℝ → ℝ) (x : ι → ℝ) :
  cfc f (Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(x i)) = Matrix.diagonal fun i => ↑(f (x i))
name: NLAlib.cfc_diagonal_real
doc:
Real functional calculus acts entrywise on a real diagonal matrix.
Arbitrary real functions are allowed because the diagonal spectrum is finite.
Source: the private `cfc_diag` proof in `JointTensorRepresentation`, via Mathlib's
diagonal algebra homomorphism and Pi CFC; Tropp 2015, §2.1.11;
atlas `golden-thompson`, `operator-monotone-convex` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_interpolate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) : cfc f A = (Polynomial.aeval A) ((Lagrange.interpolate (Finset.image hA.eigenvalues Finset.univ) id) f)
name: NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_interpolate
doc:
`f(A)` is `p(A)` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the (distinct) eigenvalues of the
symmetric `A`. Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error`
(helper; belongs in `NLAlib.Matrix.PolynomialCalculus`).

name: NLAlib.cfc_eq_aeval_of_forall_eval_eq
doc:
A matrix function of a symmetric `A` equals the polynomial calculus of any polynomial that
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues: `f(A) = p(A)` when `p(λᵢ) = f(λᵢ)` for all `i`.
Standard (Higham 2008 [`higham08`], Def. 1.4 and Thm 1.12). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper;
belongs in `NLAlib.Matrix.PolynomialCalculus`).

signature:
NLAlib.cfc_unitary_conj.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (U : ↥(unitary (Matrix ι ι ℂ))) (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) : cfc f (↑U * A * (↑U).conjTranspose) = ↑U * cfc f A * (↑U).conjTranspose
name: NLAlib.cfc_unitary_conj
doc:
Every real function on a Hermitian matrix's finite spectrum commutes with
unitary conjugation. No global continuity premise is needed. Source: Mathlib's
CFC transport and Tropp 2015, Theorem 8.5.2; atlas `golden-thompson`,
`operator-monotone-convex` (helper).

signature: NLAlib.cgObjective.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x : n → ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.cgObjective
doc:
The conjugate-gradient objective `φ(x) = ½ xᵀ A x − cᵀ x`. Its minimiser over `ℝⁿ` (for
positive definite `A`) solves `A x = c`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.6).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_add.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (c u d : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (u + d) = NLAlib.cgObjective A c u + d ⬝ᵥ (A.mulVec u - c) + NLAlib.quadForm A d / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_add
doc:
Expansion of the CG objective along a direction: for symmetric `A`,
`φ(u + d) = φ(u) + dᵀ (A u − c) + ½ dᵀ A d`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], proof of
Thm 38.2. Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c z = NLAlib.cgObjective A c xs + NLAlib.quadForm A (z - xs) / 2
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub
doc:
The CG objective measures the `A`-norm error: if `A x⋆ = c` then
`φ(z) = φ(x⋆) + ½ ‖z − x⋆‖_A²`. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], eq. (38.7).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:
NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A W : Matrix n n ℝ) (c y : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.cgObjective A c (W.mulVec y) = NLAlib.cgObjective (W.transpose * A * W) (W.transpose.mulVec c) y
name: NLAlib.cgObjective_mulVec
doc:
The CG objective under a change of variables: `φ_{A,c}(Wy) = φ_{WᵀAW, Wᵀc}(y)`.
Helper for `preconditioned-cg`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier
doc:
The gap-amplifying polynomial `chebyshevAmplifier α γ q = T_q(X/α) / T_q(1 + γ)`: equal to
`1` at `α(1 + γ)`, increasing beyond it, and exponentially small on `[−α, α]`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5; Atlas: `chebyshev-amplifier`.
atlas: chebyshev-amplifier

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def (α γ : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier α γ q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + γ) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C (1 / α) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevAmplifier_def

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (a b : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate for spectrum in `[a, b]`: the polynomial method whose residual
polynomial is `chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`,
i.e. iteration polynomial `(1 − chebyshevResidual a b q) /ₘ X`. Source: Saad (2003)
[`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: defined by its polynomial; the
three-term recurrence of Saad Alg. 12.1 is not formalised.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
  (hab : a < b) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q
name: NLAlib.chebyshevIterate_sub_mem_krylovSpace
doc:
The Chebyshev iterate lies in `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)` (its iteration polynomial has degree
`< q`). Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual
doc:
The shifted, scaled Chebyshev polynomial normalised to `1` at `0`:
`chebyshevResidual a b q = T_q((b + a − 2 X)/(b − a)) / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`. For `0 < a < b`
it has the smallest maximum modulus on `[a, b]` among polynomials of degree at most `q` with
value `1` at `0` (the residual polynomial of Chebyshev iteration and the model for CG).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: inverse-polynomial-approx

signature:
NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def (a b : ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.chebyshevResidual a b q =
    Polynomial.C (1 / Polynomial.eval ((b + a) / (b - a)) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)) *
      (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q).comp (Polynomial.C ((b + a) / (b - a)) - Polynomial.C (2 / (b - a)) * Polynomial.X)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevResidual_def

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevZero (q : ℕ) (k : Fin q) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero
doc:
The Chebyshev zeros `chebyshevZero q k = cos((2k + 1)π/(2q))`, `k < q`: the `q` roots of
`T_q`, in decreasing order. Source: Trefethen (2019) [`trefethen19`], Ch. 2 ("Chebyshev points
of the first kind"); Mathlib `Polynomial.Chebyshev.roots_T_real`.
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.
atlas: chebyshev-interpolation-error

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_injective (q : ℕ) : Function.Injective (NLAlib.chebyshevZero q)
name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_injective
doc:
The Chebyshev zeros are distinct (from Mathlib's `roots_T_real_nodup`).
Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.

signature: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_mem_Icc (q : ℕ) (k : Fin q) : NLAlib.chebyshevZero q k ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1
name: NLAlib.chebyshevZero_mem_Icc
doc: The Chebyshev zeros lie in `[−1, 1]`. Atlas: `chebyshev-interpolation-error`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient (L θ : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffCgfCoefficient
doc:
The Chernoff cgf coefficient `(e^{θL} - 1)/L`, equal to `θ` when `L = 0`. Tropp 2015, Lemma 5.4.1.
Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail (dimension : ℕ) (a L ε : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail
doc:
The matrix Chernoff lower tail `d · (e^{-ε}/(1-ε)^{1-ε})^{a/L}`, equal to `d` when `L = 0`. Tropp
2015, eq. (5.1.5). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature: NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail (dimension : ℕ) (a L ε : ℝ) : ℝ
name: NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail
doc:
The matrix Chernoff upper tail `d · (e^{ε}/(1+ε)^{1+ε})^{a/L}`, equal to `d` when `L = 0`. Tropp
2015, eq. (5.1.6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`.

signature:
NLAlib.chernoff_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)

      (∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvL ((Ψ ω).transpose * Q)) ∂μ) *

name: NLAlib.completion_reduction
doc:
**Exact Gaussian completion, deterministic reduction** (Chen–Persson, Lemma
`lem:completion`; Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Thm 5.1).

Fixed `Q` (orthonormal columns, `q ≥ 1`), its orthogonal completion `Qp = Q⊥`
(`QQᵀ + Q⊥Q⊥ᵀ = I`), fixed `A`, random `Ψ` with `s ≥ q + 2`; `G₁ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q`,
`G₂ ω = Ψ ωᵀ Q⊥`, `E = residual Q A = (I − QQᵀ)A`.
* `hG₁`: `G₁` has full column rank a.s. (so `G₁†G₁ = I`), the "almost surely" of the paper;
* `hG₂`: `E‖G₁†G₂(Q⊥ᵀE)‖_F² = E‖G₁†‖_F² · ‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F²` — `lem:moments` for `G₂` conditionally
  on `G₁` (independence of `G₁`, `G₂`) followed by the tower property;
* `hG₁m`: `E‖G₁†‖_F² = q/(s−q−1)` — `lem:invmom` (needs `s ≥ q+2`, `q ≥ 1`);
* `hGi`: integrability of the noise term.
Everything else in the paper's proof (`ΨᵀA = G₁QᵀA + G₂Q⊥ᵀE`, `X̂ = QᵀA + G₁†G₂Q⊥ᵀE`,
Pythagoras, `‖Q⊥ᵀE‖_F = ‖E‖_F`) is proved in `SketchedRegression.lean` and used here.
Conclusion: `eq:completion`,
`E‖A − Q(ΨᵀQ)†ΨᵀA‖_F² = (1 + q/(s−q−1)) ‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖_F²`.
Atlas `gn-expected-error` (helper; uses `sketched-regression`, `orthonormal-completion`).
atlas: gn-expected-error

signature:
NLAlib.coreNoise_eq.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} {r : Type u_4} {s : Type u_5}

doc:

signature:
NLAlib.covariance_rotation_eq.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} (X Y : ι → Ω → ℝ)
  (hXY : ProbabilityTheory.HasGaussianLaw (fun ω => (fun t => X t ω, fun t => Y t ω)) P)
  (hX0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), X t ω ∂P = 0) (hY0 : ∀ (t : ι), ∫ (ω : Ω), Y t ω ∂P = 0)

      (fun ω => Real.cos θ * X j ω + Real.sin θ * Y j ω) P =

doc:

process `Z(θ) = cos θ X + sin θ Y`, for jointly Gaussian centred `X, Y` with vanishing cross
moments: `Cov(Z'(θ)ᵢ, Z(θ)ⱼ) = sin θ cos θ (𝔼 YᵢYⱼ - 𝔼 XᵢXⱼ)`. Standard step of the
interpolation proofs (Vershynin 2018, proof of Thm 7.2.1). Atlas: helper of `slepian`,
`sudakov-fernique`, `gordon-minimax`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.slepian_tail_comparison` (helper `sl_cov_DZ`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsSymm) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < 2 * ↑q) :
  b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b =
    Q.transpose.mulVec b ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval (Q.transpose * A * Q)) p).mulVec (Q.transpose.mulVec b)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul
doc:
**Gauss (Lanczos) quadrature is exact for degree `< 2q`.** If `A` is symmetric, `Q` has
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, then for every polynomial `p` with
`deg p < 2q`, `bᵀ p(A) b = (Qᵀb)ᵀ p(QᵀAQ) (Qᵀb)`. Valid for every `q` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`],
Thm 2.1.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` whose range contains `K_q(A,b)`; with the Lanczos basis,
`Qᵀb = ‖b‖e₁` and the right side is `‖b‖² (p(T_q))₁₁`.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_krylovSpace_le
doc:
**Gauss (Lanczos) quadrature is exact for degree `≤ 2q − 1`** (`natDegree` form, `q ≥ 1`).
The form of `dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_of_degree_lt_two_mul` with the truncated bound
`natDegree p ≤ 2q − 1`, kept for existing callers.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Thm 6.6 and §7.1; Chen–Trogdon–Ubaru (2021) [`ctu21`],
Thm 2.1.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` whose range contains `K_q(A,b)`. The hypothesis `0 < q` is
needed here (at `q = 0` the bound `≤ 0` in ℕ admits constants and the claim fails unless
`b ∈ range Q`); the degree form needs no such hypothesis.
atlas: lanczos-gauss-quadrature

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  v ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v =

atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}

doc:
`‖p(A) v‖² = ∑ᵢ p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A`. Audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v ⬝ᵥ ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v ≤ M ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v

doc:

and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then `‖p(A) v‖² ≤ M² ‖v‖²`. Standard (Saad 2003, §6.11); audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_inv_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a c : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
  (hac : a < c) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) :
  ((cfc (fun x => 1 / x) A).mulVec b - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A (fun x => 1 / x) b) ⬝ᵥ
      ((cfc (fun x => 1 / x) A).mulVec b - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A (fun x => 1 / x) b) ≤
    (2 * (2 / a * ((√c - √a) / (√c + √a)) ^ q)) ^ 2 * b ⬝ᵥ b
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_inv_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error for `f(x) = 1/x`** (the linear-system case): if `A` is symmetric with
every eigenvalue in `[a, c]`, `0 < a < c`, then
`‖A⁻¹ b − Q (QᵀAQ)⁻¹ Qᵀ b‖ ≤ 2 (2/a) ((√c − √a)/(√c + √a))^q ‖b‖` (squared form, with
`A⁻¹ = cfc (1/x) A`). Corollary of `dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le` and
`exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le` (atlas `inverse-polynomial-approx`).
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the rate).
atlas: lanczos-fa-error (partial)

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
Eigen-expansion of a quadratic form of a matrix function: for symmetric `A`,
`vᵀ f(A) v = ∑ᵢ f(λᵢ) (uᵢ ⬝ v)²` with `(λᵢ, uᵢ)` the eigenpairs of `A`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 7, eq. (7.1). Atlas: `spectral-measure` (helper;
belongs with the polynomial calculus in `NLAlib.Matrix`).

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_self_le
doc:
**Spectral bound, `cfc` form.** If every eigenvalue of the symmetric `A` lies in `S` and
`|g| ≤ M` on `S`, then `‖g(A) v‖² ≤ M² ‖v‖²`. The `cfc` form of
`dotProduct_aeval_mulVec_self_le` (Saad 2003, §6.11). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper; the
`cfc` form of `polynomial-spectral-bound`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ}
  (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {f : ℝ → ℝ}
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < ↑q) {a c E : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c)
  (hfp : ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c, |f x - Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ E) :
  ((cfc f A).mulVec b - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A f b) ⬝ᵥ ((cfc f A).mulVec b - NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A f b) ≤
    (2 * E) ^ 2 * b ⬝ᵥ b
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_krylovFunApprox_self_le
doc:
**Lanczos-FA error bound.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in `[a, c]`, `Q` with
orthonormal columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, and `p` a polynomial with `deg p < q` and
`|f − p| ≤ E` on `[a, c]`. Then `‖f(A) b − Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b‖² ≤ (2E)² ‖b‖²`, i.e.
`‖f(A) b − Q f(T) Qᵀ b‖ ≤ 2E ‖b‖`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.4 (with Lemma 3.1);
Druskin–Knizhnerman (1989) [`dk89`]; Higham (2008) [`higham08`], §13.2.
Deviation: an arbitrary approximant `p` in place of the best one (minimise over `p` to get the
printed form); squared Euclidean norms as dot products; no `q ≥ 1` (at `q = 0`, `p = 0`).
atlas: lanczos-fa-error

NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_eq_of_apply_eq_zero.{u_2} {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] (M : Matrix k k ℝ)
