name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_eq_of_apply_eq_zero
doc:
A quadratic form at a vector supported on one index: `c ⬝ M c = c_{i₀}² M_{i₀ i₀}`.
Helper for `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_mul_dotProduct_of_eigenvalues.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {c : ℝ} (hc : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≤ c) (x : n → ℝ) :
  x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ c * x ⬝ᵥ x
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_mul_dotProduct_of_eigenvalues
doc:
Upper Rayleigh bound from an eigenvalue enclosure: `xᵀ A x ≤ c ‖x‖²` if every eigenvalue is
at most `c`. Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Thm 4.2.2. Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature`
(helper).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_mem_range.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hT : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) {θ : ℝ} (hθ : ∀ (j : k), hT.eigenvalues j ≤ θ) {y : n → ℝ}
  (hy : y ∈ Q.mulVecLin.range) : y ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y ≤ θ * y ⬝ᵥ y
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_mem_range
doc:
Rayleigh quotients over `range Q` are bounded by any upper bound `θ` on the eigenvalues of
`QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), for `Q` with orthonormal columns: `yᵀAy ≤ θ ‖y‖²` for `y ∈ range Q`.
Source: Parlett (1998), Thm 11.4.1 (Rayleigh–Ritz). Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec.{u_1} {m : Type u_1} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
  {M : Matrix m m ℝ} (hM : M.PosSemidef) {y : m → ℝ} (hy : y ⬝ᵥ y ≤ 1) {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) :
  (y ⬝ᵥ M.mulVec y) ^ s ≤ y ⬝ᵥ (M ^ s).mulVec y
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_pow_le_dotProduct_pow_mulVec
doc:
**Jensen for a positive semidefinite quadratic form.** For `M ⪰ 0`, a vector `y` with
`y ⬝ y ≤ 1` and `s ≥ 1`, `(yᵀMy)^s ≤ yᵀM^s y`. With `y = Σᵢ cᵢuᵢ` in an eigenbasis this is
`(Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ)^s ≤ Σᵢ cᵢ²λᵢ^s`, convexity of `t ↦ t^s` on `t ≥ 0` with total weight `Σᵢ cᵢ² ≤ 1`.
HMT 2011, proof of Prop 8.6. Atlas `power-iteration-deterministic` (helper; belongs in
`Matrix/PolynomialCalculus.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {σlo σhi : ℝ} (hlo : 0 < σlo) (hlohi : σlo ≤ σhi)
  (hlow : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σlo ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)
  (hup : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v ≤ σhi ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v) {b : m → ℝ} {x₀ xs x : n → ℝ}
  (hxs : A.transpose.mulVec (A.mulVec xs) = A.transpose.mulVec b) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGLSIterate A b x₀ q x) :
  A.mulVec (x - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((σhi - σlo) / (σhi + σlo)) ^ q) ^ 2 * A.mulVec (x₀ - xs) ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate
doc:
**CGLS/LSQR convergence, `κ(A)` rate.** Let `A : ℝ^{m×n}` have all singular values in
`[σ_lo, σ_hi]`, `0 < σ_lo ≤ σ_hi`, stated as `σ_lo² ‖v‖² ≤ ‖Av‖² ≤ σ_hi² ‖v‖²` for all `v` (so `A`
has full column rank), let `x⋆` solve the normal equations `AᵀA x⋆ = Aᵀb`, and `x` be a `q`-th
CGLS iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖A(x − x⋆)‖² ≤ (2((σ_hi − σ_lo)/(σ_hi + σ_lo))^q)² ‖A(x₀ − x⋆)‖²`.
Proof: CG on `AᵀA` with spectrum in `[σ_lo², σ_hi²]` (`quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3; Paige–Saunders (1982) [`ps82`].
Deviation: squared norms; the singular-value hypothesis in Rayleigh form.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

signature: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_nonneg.{u_2} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype n] (v : n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ v ⬝ᵥ v
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_nonneg
doc:
`v ⬝ᵥ v ≥ 0` for real vectors (Mathlib has only the `star` forms
`dotProduct_star_self_nonneg`). Atlas `norms-frob-spec`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_chebyshevIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

  (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q)) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q)) ≤
    (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_chebyshevIterate_le
doc:
**Chebyshev iteration, residual rate.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, `‖c − A x_q‖² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖r₀‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3. Deviation: squared norms.
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_polyIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {s : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)

    M ^ 2 * (c - A.mulVec x₀) ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_polyIterate_le
doc:
**Residual bound for a polynomial method.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `S` and
`|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`, `‖c − A x‖² ≤ M² ‖r₀‖²`. No solution is needed.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_richardsonIterate_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b ω : ℝ} (hω : 0 ≤ ω) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_self_sub_mulVec_richardsonIterate_le
doc:
**Richardson contraction, residual norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]` and
step `ω ≥ 0`, `‖c − A x_q‖² ≤ ρ^{2q} ‖r₀‖²`, `ρ = max(|1 − ωa|, |1 − ωb|)`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2. Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_le_of_isCGLSIterate.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {m : Type u_2}
  [Fintype m] {A : Matrix m n ℝ} {σlo σhi : ℝ} (hlo : 0 < σlo) (hlohi : σlo ≤ σhi)
  (hlow : ∀ (v : n → ℝ), σlo ^ 2 * v ⬝ᵥ v ≤ A.mulVec v ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec v)

doc:
**CGLS/LSQR residual bound.** Under the hypotheses of
`dotProduct_mulVec_sub_le_of_isCGLSIterate`,
`‖b − Ax‖² ≤ ‖b − Ax⋆‖² + (2((σ_hi − σ_lo)/(σ_hi + σ_lo))^q)² ‖A(x₀ − x⋆)‖²`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)
  (b : m → ℝ) (y : n → ℝ) :
  (b - A.mulVec y) ⬝ᵥ (b - A.mulVec y) = 2 * NLAlib.cgObjective (A.transpose * A) (A.transpose.mulVec b) y + b ⬝ᵥ b
name: NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq
doc:
The least-squares objective is twice the CG objective of the normal equations plus a
constant: `‖b − Ay‖² = 2 φ_{AᵀA, Aᵀb}(y) + ‖b‖²`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3.
Helper for `cgls-lsqr-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_sub_mulVec_self_eq_add.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m]

**Residual splitting for least squares.** If `x⋆` solves the normal equations
`AᵀA x⋆ = Aᵀb`, then `‖b − Ax‖² = ‖b − Ax⋆‖² + ‖A(x − x⋆)‖²` for every `x`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §8.3; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 11.1.
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.dotProduct_transpose_mul_mulVec.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

name: NLAlib.dotProduct_transpose_mul_mulVec
doc: `x ⬝ (AᵀA) x = ‖Ax‖₂²`. Atlas `norm-lipschitz`.

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_eq_dotProduct_mulVec
doc:
An eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient of its unit eigenvector: `λᵢ = uᵢᵀ A uᵢ`.
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_le_mul_tanSqAngle
doc:
**Rayleigh–Ritz step of Kaniel–Paige–Saad.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every
eigenvalue `≥ a`, `Q` with orthonormal columns, `θ₁ = θ_{j₁}` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`,
and `x ∈ range Q` with `u₁ ⬝ x ≠ 0` (`u₁ = u_{i₁}`). Then
`λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) tan² ∠(u₁, x)` (from `λ₁ − xᵀAx/xᵀx ≤ (λ₁ − a) sin² ∠(u₁, x)`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4. Helper for `kaniel-paige-saad`.

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n} {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c)
  (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues i₁) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), i ≠ i₁ → hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) (b : n → ℝ)
  (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0) (q : ℕ) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1) ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) (hT : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) {j₁ : k}
  (hj₁ : ∀ (j : k), hT.eigenvalues j ≤ hT.eigenvalues j₁) :
  hA.eigenvalues i₁ - hT.eigenvalues j₁ ≤
    (hA.eigenvalues i₁ - a) *
      (NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp b /
        Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound for the largest Ritz value.** Let `A` be real symmetric,
`λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, every other eigenvalue in `[a, c]` with `a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`),
`u₁ ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and `K_{q+1}(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (e.g. a Lanczos basis),
and `θ₁` the largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`. Then
`λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) tan² ∠(u₁, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`; the lower bound
`0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` is `eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`); Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4.
Deviation: Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`, so `T_{m−1} = T_q`); `[a, c]` any enclosure
of the other eigenvalues (Saad: `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`, factor `λ₁ − λₙ`); any orthonormal `Q`
whose range contains the Krylov space.
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le_of_poly
doc:
**Kaniel–Paige–Saad, polynomial form.** Let `A` be real symmetric with every eigenvalue
`≥ a`, `u₁ ⬝ b ≠ 0`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and `K_q(A, b) ⊆ range Q`, and `θ₁` the
largest eigenvalue of `Qᵀ A Q`. For every polynomial `p` with `deg p < q`, `p(λ₁) ≠ 0` and
`|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` for `i ≠ i₁`: `λ₁ − θ₁ ≤ (λ₁ − a) (M/p(λ₁))² tan² ∠(u₁, b)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], proof of Thm 6.4 (`i = 1`).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n}
  (htop : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≤ hA.eigenvalues i₁) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hT : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) (j : k) : hT.eigenvalues j ≤ hA.eigenvalues i₁
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le
doc:
The Ritz values are at most the top eigenvalue: `θⱼ ≤ λ_{i₁}` for every eigenvalue `θⱼ` of
`Qᵀ A Q`, `Q` with orthonormal columns. This is the lower half `0 ≤ λ₁ − θ₁` of the
Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], Thm 6.4 (left inequality; Cauchy
interlacing).
atlas: kaniel-paige-saad (partial)

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_mem_Icc
doc:
The eigenvalues of the projected matrix `Qᵀ A Q` (`Q` with orthonormal columns) lie in any
interval `[a, c]` containing the eigenvalues of `A` (Ritz values interlace inside the spectral
interval). Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 4; Parlett (1998), Thm 10.1.1 (weak form).
Atlas: `lanczos-gauss-quadrature` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (hB : B.IsHermitian) (hAB : (A + B).IsHermitian) (i j : Fin (Fintype.card n)) (hij : ↑i + ↑j < Fintype.card n) :
  hAB.eigenvalues₀ ⟨↑i + ↑j, hij⟩ ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ i + hB.eigenvalues₀ j
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le
doc:
**Weyl's inequality for eigenvalues.** For real symmetric `A`, `B`,
`λ_{i+j}(A + B) ≤ λ_i(A) + λ_j(B)` whenever `i + j < card n`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 4.3.1
(stated there increasingly; this is the decreasing, zero-indexed form). Audit G0 B7;
atlas `courant-fischer`, `weyl-mirsky`.
atlas: weyl-mirsky

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_compression_le.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {r : Type u_2} [Fintype r]
  [DecidableEq r] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n r ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (hB : (Q.transpose * A * Q).IsHermitian) (i : Fin (Fintype.card r)) :
  hB.eigenvalues₀ i ≤ hA.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.castLE ⋯ i)
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_compression_le
doc:
**Cauchy interlacing / Poincaré separation, upper bound.** For real symmetric `A` and `Q`
with orthonormal columns, the eigenvalues of the compression `B = QᵀAQ` satisfy
`λ_i(B) ≤ λ_i(A)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor 4.3.37 (Poincaré separation theorem, label to verify; the
bordered / principal-submatrix case is Thm 4.3.17). Audit G0 B8; atlas `cauchy-interlacing`.
Deviation from the audit statement: the index of `λ(A)` is `Fin.castLE` of `i`, so no side
condition `i < card n` is needed (`card r ≤ card n` is `card_le_card_of_hasOrthonormalCols`).
atlas: cauchy-interlacing

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul {n : ℕ} {S W : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hS : S.IsHermitian)
  {μ : Fin n → ℝ} (hμ : Antitone μ) (hW : W.transpose * W = 1) (hSW : S = W * Matrix.diagonal μ * W.transpose)
  (k : Fin n) : hS.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast ⋯ k) = μ k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_eq_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul
doc:
For a real symmetric `S = W diag(μ) Wᵀ` with `W` orthogonal and `μ` non-increasing, `μ` is
Mathlib's sorted eigenvalue list `eigenvalues₀` of `S` (uniqueness of the sorted spectrum, via
the characteristic polynomial). Atlas `svd` (helper; belongs with the spectral API).

name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_compression
doc:
**Cauchy interlacing / Poincaré separation, lower bound.** For real symmetric `A` and
`Q : n × r` with orthonormal columns, `λ_{i + (card n − card r)}(A) ≤ λ_i(QᵀAQ)`.
Horn–Johnson 2013, Cor 4.3.37 (label to verify). Audit G0 B8; atlas `cauchy-interlacing`.
The index bound is discharged inside the statement from `card r ≤ card n`.
atlas: cauchy-interlacing

signature:
NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_of_posSemidef_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hB : B.IsHermitian) (h : (B - A).PosSemidef) (k : Fin (Fintype.card n)) :
  hA.eigenvalues₀ k ≤ hB.eigenvalues₀ k
name: NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_of_posSemidef_sub

**Loewner monotonicity of eigenvalues.** If `B − A` is positive semidefinite then

`T_q(x) = ((x + √(x² − 1))^q + (x − √(x² − 1))^q)/2`.

of Lem. 4. Atlas: `chebyshev-growth`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_bounded_contDiff_lipschitz_approx.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) :
  ∃ F,
    (∀ (n : ℕ), ContDiff ℝ 1 (F n)) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x y : ι → ℝ), |F n x - F n y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ι → ℝ), |F n x| ≤ ↑n + 2) ∧
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ι → ℝ), |F n x| ≤ |f x| + 1) ∧

doc:
Every Euclidean Lipschitz function admits bounded smooth approximants preserving its
Lipschitz constant. They converge pointwise and satisfy `|fₙ|≤|f|+1`, so once `f` is
integrable the means converge by dominated convergence. Clamping is performed before
mollification. Ledoux 2001, proof of Theorem 5.3; atlas `herbst` (approximation helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_contDiff_abs_sub_le_of_lipschitz.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
  (hLip : ∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |f x - f y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ g,
    (∀ (n : ℕ), ContDiff ℝ (↑n) g) ∧
      (∀ (x y : ι → ℝ), |g x - g y| ≤ L * √(∑ i, (x i - y i) ^ 2)) ∧ ∀ (x : ι → ℝ), |g x - f x| ≤ ε
name: NLAlib.exists_contDiff_abs_sub_le_of_lipschitz
doc:
**Smooth approximation of Lipschitz functions**: an `L`-Lipschitz (Euclidean) function
`f : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ` is within `ε` of a `C^∞` function that is again `L`-Lipschitz (mollify with a
normed bump of small support). Source: standard; Ledoux, *Concentration of Measure*, §5.1.
Atlas: `gaussian-concentration` (helper). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.lipschitz_smooth_approx`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_le_eval_eq_one_abs_eval_le {a c L : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hcL : c < L) (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ p,
    p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧
      Polynomial.eval L p = 1 ∧
        ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a c,
          |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ 1 / Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((L - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q)
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_le_eval_eq_one_abs_eval_le
doc:
**The shifted Chebyshev amplifier.** For `a < c < L` and every `q` there is a polynomial
`p` of degree at most `q` with `p(L) = 1` and `|p| ≤ 1/T_q(1 + 2γ)` on `[a, c]`,
`γ = (L − c)/(c − a)`: namely `p(x) = T_q((2x − c − a)/(c − a))/T_q(1 + 2γ)`, the
`chebyshevAmplifier` with `α = (c − a)/2`, `γ' = 2γ`, shifted by `(c + a)/2`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1. Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (belongs in
`NLAlib.Polynomial.Approximation` next to `chebyshev-amplifier`).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le {a b : ℝ} (q : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) :
  ∃ p, p.degree < ↑q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, |Polynomial.eval x p - 1 / x| ≤ 2 / a * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_abs_eval_sub_inv_le
doc:
Polynomial approximation of `1/x` on `[a, b]`: for `0 < a < b` there is a polynomial `p` of
degree `< q` with `|p(x) − 1/x| ≤ (2/a)((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q` on `[a, b]`. The polynomial is
`p = (1 − r)/X` for the Chebyshev residual `r = chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8 (the CG error bound). Atlas:
`inverse-polynomial-approx`.
atlas: inverse-polynomial-approx

signature:
NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul_of_eval_zero_eq_one {p : Polynomial ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) : ∃ s, s.degree < ↑q ∧ 1 - p = Polynomial.X * s
name: NLAlib.exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul_of_eval_zero_eq_one
doc:
**Residual-polynomial factorisation.** If `deg p ≤ q` and `p(0) = 1`, then `1 − p = X s` for
some `s` with `deg s < q`. This is the algebra behind every residual-polynomial Krylov argument:
`x₀ + s(A) r₀ ∈ x₀ + K_q` has error `p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11
(the set `P_q^0`); Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35. Promoted from the private CG lemma
`exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul` (atlas `residual-polynomial`, helper).

name: NLAlib.exists_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_ge
doc:
**Gap-free Ritz-value bound.** Let `A` be symmetric with eigenvalues in `[0, λ₁]`,
`λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, `0 < ε < 1`, `q ≥ 1`, `u_{i₁} ⬝ b ≠ 0`, and `Q` with orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A, b) ⊆ range Q` (e.g. the Lanczos basis). Then some Ritz value `θ_j` (eigenvalue of
`QᵀAQ`) satisfies
`λ₁ − θ_j ≤ ε λ₁ + λ₁ (2/(1 + √(2γ))^{q−1})² ‖b‖²/(u_{i₁} ⬝ b)²`, `γ = ε/(1 − ε)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Thm 1 (single-vector, gap-free); Kuczyński–Woźniakowski
(1992) [`kw92`] for the random-start analysis. Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds`; uses
`chebyshev-amplifier`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`, `krylov-subspace`.
Label note: this is the gap-free bound (MM15); the gap-dependent bound of Saad (2011), Thm 6.4,
is `eigenvalues_sub_eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_le` (`kaniel-paige-saad`).
atlas: ritz-value-bounds

signature:
NLAlib.exists_eq_transpose_mul_of_posSemidef.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.PosSemidef) : ∃ F, A = F.transpose * F
name: NLAlib.exists_eq_transpose_mul_of_posSemidef
doc:
A real positive semidefinite matrix is a Gram matrix: `A = FᵀF` for some square `F`.
Mathlib `CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self`. Atlas `nystrom-structural` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_finset_net_specNorm_le.{u_3, u_4} (n : Type u_3) [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε)
  (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  ∃ N,
    (∀ x ∈ N, x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) ∧
      ↑N.card ≤ (1 + 2 / ε) ^ Fintype.card n ∧
        ∀ (m : Type u_4) [inst : Fintype m] [inst_1 : DecidableEq m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (M : ℝ),
          0 ≤ M → (∀ x ∈ N, √(A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x) ≤ M) → NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ M / (1 - ε)
name: NLAlib.exists_finset_net_specNorm_le
doc:
**ε-net bound for the spectral norm.** For `0 < ε < 1` there is a set `N` of at most
`(1 + 2/ε)^{card n}` unit vectors of `ℝ^n` such that for every real matrix `A` with `n` columns
and every `M ≥ 0`, `‖Ax‖₂ ≤ M` on `N` implies `‖A‖₂ ≤ M/(1-ε)`.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.2–5.3; Vershynin 2018, Cor 4.2.13 and Ex 4.4.3; audit G1 B1.
Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`. Deviation: the atlas states `(1-2ε)⁻¹`; the standard (and stronger)
operator form `(1-ε)⁻¹` is used here, the `(1-2ε)⁻¹` forms being
`specNorm_le_div_of_net_bilinear` and `specNorm_le_div_of_net_quadForm`.
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:
NLAlib.exists_finset_sphere_net.{u_3} (ι : Type u_3) [Fintype ι] {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ N,
    (∀ x ∈ N, x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) ∧
      ↑N.card ≤ (1 + 2 / ε) ^ Fintype.card ι ∧ ∀ (y : ι → ℝ), y ⬝ᵥ y = 1 → ∃ x ∈ N, (x - y) ⬝ᵥ (x - y) ≤ ε ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_finset_sphere_net
doc:
**Volumetric ε-net of the sphere.** For `ε > 0`, the unit sphere of `ℝ^ι` (Euclidean) has an
`ε`-net contained in the sphere with at most `(1 + 2/ε)^{card ι}` points:
`∀ y` with `yᵀy = 1`, `∃ x ∈ N`, `(x - y)ᵀ(x - y) ≤ ε²`. For an empty index type the sphere is
empty and `N = ∅`. Proof: a maximal `ε`-separated subset of the sphere is an `ε`-net, and the
volumetric packing bound caps the size of every separated subset.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.2; Vershynin 2018, Cor 4.2.13; audit G1 A1. Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`
(covering half). Deviation: index type any `[Fintype ι]` (audit: `Fin n`).
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:

with a nonnegative antitone measurable factor. No density premise is assumed.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iInf_sqrt_mulVec_le_of_sigmaMin_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

  ∃ j, ⨅ x, √(A.mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec ↑x) ≤ √↑(Fintype.card n) * s
name: NLAlib.exists_iInf_sqrt_mulVec_le_of_sigmaMin_le
doc:
**Small `σ_min` forces a column close to the span of the others.** For `A : Matrix m n ℝ`
with `n` nonempty, if `σ_min(A) ≤ s` then for some column `j`,
`inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 } ≤ √|n| · s`; the left side is the distance from column `j` to the
span of the other columns.

"invertibility via distance" step). Atlas: `smin-small-ball`. Generalised from
`Fin N × Fin n` (with `1 ≤ n`) to arbitrary finite index types with `n` nonempty. Ported from
Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.sMin_le_imp_dist_le`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef)
  (c x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) : ∃ x, NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x
name: NLAlib.exists_isCGIterate
doc:
**Existence of the CG iterate.** For positive definite `A`, every `c`, `x₀` and `q`, there
is a `q`-th CG iterate. It is the Galerkin solution: the bilinear form `(y, z) ↦ zᵀ A y` on `K_q`
is nondegenerate, hence `y ↦ (z ↦ zᵀ A y)` is a bijection `K_q → K_q*`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2 (uniqueness and existence of the minimiser).
Atlas: `cg-convergence`.
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isGMRESIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : ∃ x, NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x
name: NLAlib.exists_isGMRESIterate
doc:
**Existence.** For every square `A`, right-hand side `c`, start `x₀` and `q` there is a
GMRES iterate (a least-squares problem over `A K_q`; no hypothesis on `A`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.5.1; Saad–Schultz (1986) [`ss86`], §2.
atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isGradedKrylovBasis_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ)
  (q : ℕ) : (∃ Q, NLAlib.IsGradedKrylovBasis A b Q) ↔ q ≤ NLAlib.krylovGrade A b
name: NLAlib.exists_isGradedKrylovBasis_iff
doc:
**Existence of graded bases**: a graded orthonormal Krylov basis with `q` columns exists iff
`q ≤ krylovGrade A b`. Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.3; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop. 6.4.
atlas: graded-krylov-basis-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isMoorePenroseInverse.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  (A : Matrix m n ℝ) : ∃ B, NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse A B
name: NLAlib.exists_isMoorePenroseInverse
doc:
Every real rectangular matrix has a Moore–Penrose inverse, with arbitrary
finite row and column types and without a rank or nonempty assumption.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature: NLAlib.exists_isSVD {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ U V, NLAlib.IsSVD A U V
name: NLAlib.exists_isSVD
doc:
**Singular value decomposition** (Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 2.6.3; HMT 2011, §2.1): every real
`m × n` matrix is `A = U Σ Vᵀ` with `U`, `V` orthogonal and `Σ = rectDiag (singularValues A)`,
the singular values being nonnegative and non-increasing (`singularValues_nonneg`,
`singularValues_antitone`). Atlas `svd`.

Proof: `V` is an orthonormal eigenbasis of `AᵀA` (Mathlib's spectral theorem, sorted), the
vectors `A vⱼ / σⱼ` with `σⱼ ≠ 0` are orthonormal and are completed to an orthonormal basis of
`ℝᵐ` (atlas `orthonormal-completion`) giving `U`.
atlas: svd

signature:
NLAlib.exists_isSymm_transpose_mul_mul_eq_one.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {P : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hP : P.PosDef) : ∃ W, W.IsSymm ∧ W.transpose * P * W = 1
name: NLAlib.exists_isSymm_transpose_mul_mul_eq_one
doc:
A positive definite `P` has a symmetric inverse square root: some `W = Wᵀ` with
`Wᵀ P W = I` (`W = P^{-1/2} = U diag(λ^{-1/2}) Uᵀ`). Source: Horn–Johnson (2013), Thm 7.2.6.
Helper for `preconditioned-cg` (belongs in `NLAlib.Matrix`).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {s : Finset ℝ} (hs : s.card = q + 2)
  (hsab : ∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_card
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem**, finset form: if `f` vanishes on a set of `q + 2` points of
`[a, b]` (hypotheses as in `exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono`), then `f^{(q+1)}`
vanishes somewhere in `(a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, proof of Thm 6.2. Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} {q : ℕ} {v : Fin (q + 2) → ℝ}
  (hv : StrictMono v) (hva : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), v i ∈ Set.Icc a b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ k < q, ContinuousOn (iteratedDeriv (k + 1) f) (Set.Ioo a b)) (hz : ∀ (i : Fin (q + 2)), f (v i) = 0) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b, iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ = 0
name: NLAlib.exists_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_strictMono
doc:
**Generalised Rolle theorem.** If `f` vanishes at `q + 2` points `v 0 < ⋯ < v (q+1)` of
`[a, b]`, `f` is continuous on `[a, b]` and the derivatives `f', …, f^{(q)}` are continuous on
`(a, b)`, then `f^{(q+1)}(ξ) = 0` for some `ξ ∈ (a, b)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, proof of Thm 6.2; Atkinson,
*An Introduction to Numerical Analysis* (2nd ed.), proof of Thm 3.2.
Atlas: `interpolation-remainder` (lemma).
Deviation: stated with `q + 2` zeros and the `(q + 1)`-st derivative (so the conclusion is in the
open interval without a side condition); only continuity of `f^{(k)}`, `1 ≤ k ≤ q`, on `(a, b)`
is assumed — no differentiability, because `iteratedDeriv` is Mathlib's global derivative and
Rolle (`exists_deriv_eq_zero`) needs only continuity.
atlas: interpolation-remainder

signature:
NLAlib.exists_measurable_extension_of_antitoneOn_Ioi (ℓ : ℝ) (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : AntitoneOn h (Set.Ioi ℓ)) :
  ∃ h', Measurable h' ∧ Set.EqOn h' h (Set.Ioi ℓ)
name: NLAlib.exists_measurable_extension_of_antitoneOn_Ioi
doc:
An antitone representative on a real half-line has a globally measurable
extension agreeing with it on that half-line. Source: operator rederivations,
Section 5, density API; atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_measurable_gaussian_range_frame {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (t : ℕ) :
  ∃ Qf,
    (∀ (i : Fin m) (j : Fin (min A.rank t)), Measurable fun G => Qf G i j) ∧
      (∀ᵐ (G : Fin n → Fin t → ℝ) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t, NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols (Qf G)) ∧
        ∀ᵐ (G : Fin n → Fin t → ℝ) ∂NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t,
          Qf G * ((Qf G).transpose * (A * Matrix.of G)) = A * Matrix.of G
name: NLAlib.exists_measurable_gaussian_range_frame
doc:
A fixed matrix and Gaussian sketch width admit a constructed entrywise measurable
orthonormal range frame of `min(rank A,t)` columns almost surely. The full-column branch
uses the polar map; the rank-deficient branch uses a fixed frame of `range A`. Thus no
measurable-frame certificate has to be assumed in normalized Gaussian algorithms.
HMT 2011, §10.2; atlas `rsvd-expected-error`, `gn-expected-error`.

signature:
NLAlib.exists_measure_restrict_le_smul_volume_of_weak_deriv_nonneg (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ) [μ.Regular] (ℓ a : ℝ)

name: NLAlib.exists_measure_restrict_le_smul_volume_of_weak_deriv_nonneg

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_add_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q)
  (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  ∃ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q, x₀ + y - xs = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_add_sub_eq_aeval_mulVec
doc:
**Error form, converse.** If `A x⋆ = c`, every residual polynomial `p` is realised:
some `y ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` has `x₀ + y − x⋆ = p(A)(x₀ − x⋆)`. No hypothesis on `A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c x₀ : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree ≤ ↑q) (hp0 : Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1) :
  ∃ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q,
    c - A.mulVec (x₀ + y) = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec
doc:
**Every residual polynomial is realised in `x₀ + K_q`.** For `deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1` there
is `y ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` with `c − A (x₀ + y) = p(A) r₀`. No hypothesis on `A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial: converse).
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_rayleigh_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hpsd : ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues i) {i₁ : n}
  (htop : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ≤ hA.eigenvalues i₁) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ}
  (hq : 0 < q) (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0) :
  ∃ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q,
    y ≠ 0 ∧
      hA.eigenvalues i₁ * y ⬝ᵥ y - y ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec y ≤
        (ε * hA.eigenvalues i₁ +
            hA.eigenvalues i₁ * (2 / (1 + √(2 * (ε / (1 - ε)))) ^ (q - 1)) ^ 2 * b ⬝ᵥ b /
              ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b) ^ 2) *
          y ⬝ᵥ y
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_sub_rayleigh_le
doc:
**A Krylov vector with near-maximal Rayleigh quotient (gap-free).** Let `A` be symmetric
with eigenvalues in `[0, λ₁]`, `λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, let `0 < ε < 1`, `q ≥ 1`, and `c₁ = u_{i₁} ⬝ b ≠ 0`.
Then there is a nonzero `y ∈ K_q(A, b)` with
`λ₁ ‖y‖² − yᵀAy ≤ (ε λ₁ + λ₁ (2/(1 + √(2γ))^{q−1})² ‖b‖²/c₁²) ‖y‖²`, `γ = ε/(1 − ε)`.
Source: Musco–Musco (2015) [`mm15`], Lem. 4–5 and proof of Thm 1 (single-vector case).
Atlas: `ritz-value-bounds`; uses `chebyshev-amplifier`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`krylov-subspace`.
atlas: ritz-value-bounds

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n} {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues i₁)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), i ≠ i₁ → hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) (b : n → ℝ) (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0)
  (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1),
    (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp x ≤
        NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp b /
          Polynomial.eval (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a))) (Polynomial.Chebyshev.T ℝ ↑q) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le
doc:
**Angle between the top eigenvector and the Krylov space (Chebyshev bound).** Let `A` be
real symmetric, `λ₁ = λ_{i₁}`, and suppose every other eigenvalue lies in `[a, c]` with
`a < c < λ₁` (e.g. `a = λₙ`, `c = λ₂`). If `u₁ ⬝ b ≠ 0` then `K_{q+1}(A, b)` contains `x` with
`u₁ ⬝ x ≠ 0` and `tan² ∠(u₁, x) ≤ tan² ∠(u₁, b) / T_q(1 + 2γ)²`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`.
The witness is `x = T_q((2A − (c + a)I)/(c − a)) b`, written through `chebyshevAmplifier`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1 (case `i = 1`); Saad (2003), §6.11.
Deviation: squared tangents; Krylov dimension `q + 1` (Saad's `m`) so that the degree is `q`;
an arbitrary enclosure `[a, c]` of the other eigenvalues instead of `[λₙ, λ₂]`.
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle

signature:
NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le_two_div_pow.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {i₁ : n} {a c : ℝ} (hac : a < c) (hc : c < hA.eigenvalues i₁)
  (hspec : ∀ (i : n), i ≠ i₁ → hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a c) (b : n → ℝ) (hb : (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ b ≠ 0)
  (q : ℕ) :
  ∃ x ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A b (q + 1),
    (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp ⬝ᵥ x ≠ 0 ∧
      NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp x ≤
        (2 /
              (1 + 2 * ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a)) +
                  2 * √((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a) + ((hA.eigenvalues i₁ - c) / (c - a)) ^ 2)) ^
                q) ^
            2 *
          NLAlib.tanSqAngle (hA.eigenvectorBasis i₁).ofLp b
name: NLAlib.exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le_two_div_pow
doc:
**Eigenvector angle, explicit rate.** Under the hypotheses of
`exists_mem_krylovSpace_tanSqAngle_le`, `K_{q+1}(A, b)` contains `x` with `u₁ ⬝ x ≠ 0` and
`tan² ∠(u₁, x) ≤ (2/(1 + 2γ + 2√(γ + γ²))^q)² tan² ∠(u₁, b)`, `γ = (λ₁ − c)/(c − a)`.
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1.
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle

signature:
NLAlib.exists_nonneg_primitive_of_ordered_supports (c a b : ℝ) (hca : c < a) (hab : a < b) (f g : ℝ → ℝ)
  (hf : ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) f) (hg : ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) g) (hfc : HasCompactSupport f) (hgc : HasCompactSupport g)
  (hfs : tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b) (hgs : tsupport g ⊆ Set.Ioo c a) (hf0 : ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ f x)

doc:
Two nonnegative smooth functions with disjoint ordered supports and equal total

Source: operator rederivations, Section 5, interval alternative to mollification;
atlas wishart-lambda-min-tail (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthogonal_completion.{u_4} {k : ℕ} {ι : Type u_4} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (V : Matrix (Fin k) ι ℝ)

doc:
Every fixed real matrix has an orthonormal frame of exactly `rank A` columns
whose projector reproduces `A`. The frame may be chosen once for that fixed input;
no measurable choice as `A` varies is claimed. Zero-rank matrices are included.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `gn-expected-error` (rank-deficient sketch branch).

signature:
NLAlib.exists_orthonormal_ker_sq_dist_rowSpace {n k : ℕ} (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hH : H.rank = n) :
  ∃ V,
    V.transpose * V = 1 ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin (k - n)), (H.mulVec fun l => V l j) = 0) ∧
        ∀ (g : Fin k → ℝ),
          g ⬝ᵥ g - H.mulVec g ⬝ᵥ (H * H.transpose)⁻¹.mulVec (H.mulVec g) = ∑ j, V.transpose.mulVec g j ^ 2
name: NLAlib.exists_orthonormal_ker_sq_dist_rowSpace
doc:
**Residual in an orthonormal basis of the kernel.** For `H` of full row rank `n`, an
orthonormal basis `V` (`k × (k - n)`, `Vᵀ V = 1`) of `ker H` writes the squared distance from `g`

killed by `H`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5 (law of the residual of a Gaussian
row and its independence from the regression). Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean` (helper). Ported
from the Prove2me solutions `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law` and
`GaussianMatrix.regression_residual_indep` (the two copies merged, keeping the stronger
statement).

  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ k ≤ q, DifferentiableOn ℝ (iteratedDeriv k f) (Set.Ioo a b)) :
  ∃ ξ ∈ Set.Ioo a b,
    f x - Polynomial.eval x ((Lagrange.interpolate Finset.univ v) (f ∘ v)) =
      iteratedDeriv (q + 1) f ξ / ↑(q + 1).factorial * Polynomial.eval x (Lagrange.nodal Finset.univ v)
name: NLAlib.exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq
doc:
**Interpolation remainder formula.** Let `v : Fin (q + 1) → ℝ` be distinct nodes in
`[a, b]`, `f` continuous on `[a, b]` with `f, f', …, f^{(q)}` differentiable on `(a, b)`, and
`x ∈ [a, b]`. Then for the interpolating polynomial `L = Lagrange.interpolate univ v (f ∘ v)`
and the nodal polynomial `ω = ∏ (X − v i)` there is `ξ ∈ (a, b)` with
`f x − L(x) = f^{(q+1)}(ξ) / (q + 1)! · ω(x)`.
Source: Süli–Mayers, *An Introduction to Numerical Analysis*, Thm 6.2; Atkinson (2nd ed.),
Thm 3.2; Cheney, *Introduction to Approximation Theory*, Ch. 3. Atlas:
`interpolation-remainder`.
Deviation: `ξ` is in the open interval `(a, b)` (stronger than `[a, b]`), at the cost of the
hypothesis `a < b` (used only when `x` is a node).
atlas: interpolation-remainder

[`tb97`], Lect. 35. Atlas: `residual-polynomial` (partial: forward direction).

      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧

doc:
Every actual real matrix has an SVD-derived right-space block split whose
tail is the genuine optimal squared rank-`k` error. The head singular values
are absorbed into `U₁=A V₁`, as permitted by HMT's structural lemma.
Only `k≤n` is needed; `k>m` is handled by the padded zero singular values.
HMT 2011, Theorem 9.1; atlas `rsvd-expected-error`, `gn-expected-error`.

    A = U₁ * 1 * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose ∧
      NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂ ∧
        NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁ ∧
          NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂ ∧

doc:

`A = U₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ` with `U₂`, `V₁`, `V₂` orthonormal, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`, `‖Σ₂‖ = σ_{k+1}` and
`‖Σ₂‖_F² = ∑_{j>k} σ_j²` (zero-indexed `singularValues A k`, `singularValueTailSq A k`). The
blocks are those of `exists_svd_right_blocks` (`U₁ = AV₁`, `U₂ = U`), with the spectral tail
identified through `IsSVD.specNorm_sub_truncatedMatrix`. HMT 2011, §2.1 and Thm 9.1.
Atlas `rsvd-spectral-expected` (helper; uses `svd`, `eckart-young`; belongs in
`Matrix/SvdBlocks.lean`).

signature:
NLAlib.frobInner_le_sqrt_mul_frobNorm_mul_specNorm_of_rank_le.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m]
  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] {r : ℕ} (X E : Matrix m n ℝ) (hX : X.rank ≤ r) :
  NLAlib.frobInner X E ≤ √↑r * NLAlib.frobNorm X * NLAlib.specNorm E
name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_sqrt_mul_frobNorm_mul_specNorm_of_rank_le
doc:
**Rank corollary of the von Neumann trace inequality.** If `rank X ≤ r` then
`⟨X, E⟩_F ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`. Proof: with the orthogonal projector `P = X X⁺` onto `range X`,
`⟨X, E⟩_F = ⟨X, P E⟩_F ≤ ‖X‖_F ‖P E‖_F ≤ ‖X‖_F √(rank P E) ‖P E‖₂ ≤ √r ‖X‖_F ‖E‖₂`.
It follows from Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.1.1 (von Neumann) and Cauchy–Schwarz over the top
`r` singular values; this is the `VonNeumannRankBound` hypothesis of the Chen–Persson LRA
formalization. Audit G0 C4; atlas `von-neumann-trace` (rank corollary). Deviation: arbitrary
finite index types, no full-rank or nonemptiness condition.
atlas: von-neumann-rank-bound

name: NLAlib.frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul
doc:
**Von Neumann trace inequality.** For real `m × n` matrices,
`⟨X, E⟩_F = tr(XᵀE) ≤ ∑_{k < min m n} σ_k(X) σ_k(E)`. Horn–Johnson 2013, Thm 7.4.1.1 (real case,
`Re tr(X E*) = frobInner X E`); Mirsky 1975. Proof: Ky Fan's maximum principle for the diagonal
of `UᵀEV` (through the weighted top-`k` inequality `sum_mul_le_sum_ite_lt_of_antitone`) and
Abel summation over `σ(X)`; no Birkhoff theorem is needed. Audit G0 A2;
atlas `von-neumann-trace`.
atlas: von-neumann-trace

case): if `A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and

hypotheses the proof uses (`U₂ᵀU₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality,
no conditions on `U₁`); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`
(HMT take `range Q = range(AΩ)`); index types are arbitrary `Fintype`s. Atlas
`hmt-9-1-frobenius`.

signature:
NLAlib.gammaRatio_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) :
  2 ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1)) ≤
    ((↑k + ↑r) / 2) ^ ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2) / (2 * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1))
name: NLAlib.gammaRatio_le
doc:
**Gamma-ratio estimate.** For `1 ≤ r ≤ k`,
`2^{(k-r-1)/2} Γ((k+1)/2) / (Γ(r/2) Γ(k-r+1)) ≤ ((k+r)/2)^{(k-r+1)/2} / (2 Γ(k-r+1))`,
i.e. the constant of the density bound (B.5) is at most the constant of (B.6).

Tropp–Webber 2023, (B.6). Atlas: `wishart-lambda-min-tail` (helper). Proof: iterated Gautschi
inequality (log-convexity of `Γ`, Bohr–Mollerup) and AM–GM (`prod_range_add_le_pow`). Ported
from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.tw_gamma_ratio_bound`.
atlas: wishart-lambda-min-tail

signature:
NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r < k) :
  2 ^ (-(↑k - ↑r) / 2) * Real.pi * Real.Gamma (↑k / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k - ↑r + 1) / 2) ^ 2) ≤
    (Real.exp 1 ^ 2 * (↑k + ↑r - 1) / (2 * (↑k - ↑r) ^ 2)) ^ ((↑k - ↑r) / 2)
name: NLAlib.gamma_inverse_spectral_endpoint_le
doc:
The endpoint quadratic-probe constant for an `r × k` Gaussian matrix
is bounded by the strengthened inverse spectral moment constant.
Source: direct quadratic-probe proof, endpoint moment calculation; the
arithmetic-progression mean retains `k+r-1`. Atlas:
`inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gamma_probe_mellin_residue_eq (x α : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) (hα : 0 < α) :
  Real.Gamma (x + α) * √Real.pi / (2 ^ α * Real.Gamma x * Real.Gamma α * Real.Gamma (α + 1 / 2)) =
    2 ^ (α - 1) * Real.Gamma (x + α) / (Real.Gamma x * Real.Gamma (2 * α))
name: NLAlib.gamma_probe_mellin_residue_eq
doc:
Duplication turns the operator Mellin residue into the hard-edge density constant.
Source: Legendre duplication, operator rederivations Section 5; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (exact constant helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_ae_hasOrthonormalCols_gaussianRangeFrame {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (t : ℕ) :

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_ae_isUnit_gram_mul_of_le_rank {m n t : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (ht : t ≤ A.rank) :

atlas: gaussian-full-rank-ae

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_ae_project_gaussianRangeFrame {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (t : ℕ) :

doc:
The projector of the constructed Gaussian range frame reproduces the first

NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_ae_rank_eq (p m : ℕ) :

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_ae_rank_mul_eq_min {m n t : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_eq_map_curry (p m : ℕ) :

      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_eq_map_curry
doc:
A standard Gaussian matrix is the currying of i.i.d. standard Gaussians indexed by
`Fin p × Fin m` (the converse of `gaussianMatrix_map_uncurry`). Atlas: `gaussian-matrix-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_indepFun_block {n k r t : ℕ} (V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (V₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin r) ℝ)
  (hV₁ : V₁.transpose * V₁ = 1) (hV₂ : V₂.transpose * V₂ = 1) (hV₁₂ : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) :
  ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (V₁.transpose * Matrix.of G))
    (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (V₂.transpose * Matrix.of G)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t)
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_indepFun_block
doc:
**Independence of Gaussian blocks.** If `V₁` (`n × k`) and `V₂` (`n × r`) have orthonormal
columns and `V₁ᵀ V₂ = 0`, and `G` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix, then `V₁ᵀ G` and
`V₂ᵀ G` are independent.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), §10.2 (`Ω₁ = V₁ᵀ Ω` and `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀ Ω` are independent).
Atlas: `block-law-indep`. Ported from the Prove2me workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices
series.
atlas: block-law-indep

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r + 4 ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) {G | 12 * ↑r / (↑k - ↑r) * t < NLAlib.frobSq (NLAlib.pinvR (Matrix.of G))} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (4 * t ^ (-((↑k - ↑r) / 2)))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_frobSq_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the Frobenius norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `r + 4 ≤ k` and `t ≥ 1`,
`P[‖G†‖_F² > 12 r t/(k-r)] ≤ 4 t^{-(k-r)/2}`, with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Thm A.6 (used in Prop 10.4; HMT state it as `P[‖Ω₁†‖_F ≥ √(12k/p) t] ≤ 4 t^{-p}`
with `Ω₁` of size `k × (k+p)`, the same bound after `t ↦ √t`). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`.
Proof: each diagonal entry of `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹` is `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`
(`gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), whose `L^{(k-r)/2}` norm is at most
`3/(k-r+1)` (`integrable_and_integral_rpow_inv_sum_sq_gaussianReal_lt`, atlas
`chi-square-neg-moment`); Minkowski's inequality bounds `‖tr (G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖_{L^q}` and Markov's
inequality gives the tail. Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.pinv_frobenius_tail`.
atlas: pinv-frob-tail

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le {r k : ℕ} (hr : 2 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) {G | t < NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.pinvR (Matrix.of G))} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal
      (1 / √(2 * Real.pi * (↑k - ↑r + 1)) * (Real.exp 1 * √↑k / (↑k - ↑r + 1)) ^ (↑k - ↑r + 1) * t ^ (-(↑k - ↑r + 1)))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_lt_specNorm_pinvR_le
doc:
**Tail bound for the spectral norm of the Gaussian pseudoinverse.** For an `r × k`
standard Gaussian matrix `G` with `2 ≤ r ≤ k` and `t > 0`,
`P[‖G†‖ > t] ≤ (2π(k-r+1))^{-1/2} (e√k/(k-r+1))^{k-r+1} t^{-(k-r+1)}`,
with `G† = pinvR G`.

HMT 2011, Prop A.3; Chen–Dongarra 2005, Lemma 4.1. Atlas: `pinv-spectral-tail`. Proof:
`‖G†‖² = ‖(G Gᵀ)⁻¹‖ = 1/σ_min(Gᵀ)²` (`specNorm_pinvR_sq`,
`specNorm_inv_self_mul_transpose_eq`, atlas `pseudoinverse`), the `λ_min` lower tail
(`gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le`, atlas `wishart-lambda-min-tail`, which uses the
proved operator bound (B.5)) and Stirling's formula. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.pinv_spectral_tail`.
atlas: pinv-spectral-tail

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_block {n k t : ℕ} (V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ) (hV₁ : V₁.transpose * V₁ = 1) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (V₁.transpose * Matrix.of G)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) =
    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k t
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_block
doc:
**Law of a Gaussian block.** If `V₁` (`n × k`) has orthonormal columns and `G` is an
`n × t` standard Gaussian matrix, then `V₁ᵀ G` is a `k × t` standard Gaussian matrix.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), §10.2 (with `G = Ω` and `V₁` the leading right singular
vectors: `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀ Ω` is standard Gaussian). Atlas: `block-law-indep`. Ported from the Prove2me
workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices series.
atlas: block-law-indep

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_first_cols (n : ℕ) {q t : ℕ} (hqt : q ≤ t) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G i j => G i (Fin.castLE hqt j)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) =
    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n q
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_first_cols
doc:
Selecting the first `q` columns of an `n×t` standard Gaussian matrix gives the
`n×q` standard Gaussian law. HMT 2011, §10.2; atlas `gaussian-matrix-def`,
`gn-expected-error` (rank-deficient first-sketch helper).

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self {r k : ℕ} (hrk : r ≤ k) (i : Fin r) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => (Matrix.of G * (Matrix.of G).transpose)⁻¹ i i) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x => (∑ j, x j ^ 2)⁻¹)
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self
doc:
**Law of a diagonal entry of the inverse Wishart matrix.** For an `r × k` standard Gaussian
matrix `G` with `r ≤ k` and any `i`, `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ` has the law of `1/χ²_{k-r+1}`, i.e. of
`(∑ⱼ xⱼ²)⁻¹` for a standard Gaussian vector `x ∈ ℝ^{k-r+1}`.

HMT 2011, proof of Prop A.5 / Tropp–Webber 2023, proof of Lemma B.2 (each diagonal entry of an
inverse Wishart matrix is an inverse chi-square). Atlas: `pinv-frob-tail`,
`inverse-wishart-frob-moment` (helper). Proof: Schur complement
(`inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`), conditioning on the other rows, which have full rank
a.s. (`gaussianMatrix_ae_rank_eq`, atlas `gaussian-full-rank-ae`), and the residual law
(`pi_gaussianReal_map_sq_dist_rowSpace`, atlas `block-law-indep`). Ported from Prove2me
solution `GaussianMatrix.inverse_wishart_diag_law`.

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec {k n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => (Matrix.of G).mulVec x) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x_1 => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 (x ⬝ᵥ x).toNNReal
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec
doc:
**Law of `G x`.** If `G` is a `k × n` standard Gaussian matrix and `x ∈ ℝⁿ`, then the
coordinates of `G x` are i.i.d. `N(0, ‖x‖²)`.

HMT 2011, §10.1. Atlas: `gaussian-matrix-mulVec-law` (audit G1 C3). The variance is written
`(x ⬝ᵥ x).toNNReal`; for `x = 0` both sides are the Dirac mass at `0`. Proof: the unit-vector case
`gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec_of_dotProduct_self_eq_one` and Mathlib `gaussianReal_map_const_mul`.
atlas: gaussian-matrix-mulvec-law

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec_of_dotProduct_self_eq_one {k n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) (hx : x ⬝ᵥ x = 1) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => (Matrix.of G).mulVec x) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n) =
    MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_mulVec_of_dotProduct_self_eq_one
doc:
**Law of `G x` for a unit vector.** If `G` is a `k × n` standard Gaussian matrix and
`x ⬝ᵥ x = 1`, then `G x` is a standard Gaussian vector in `ℝᵏ`.

HMT 2011, §10.1; Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, proof of Lem 2.2 (`‖G x‖² ∼ χ²_k`). Atlas:
`gaussian-matrix-mulVec-law` (audit G1 C3 / G2 C1(d)). Proof: `gaussianMatrix_map_mul_right`
with the one-column matrix `x`.
atlas: gaussian-matrix-mulvec-law

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_mul_right {k m d : ℕ} (U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin d) ℝ) (hU : U.transpose * U = 1) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (Matrix.of G * U)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k m) =
    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k d
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_mul_right
doc:
**Right multiplication by orthonormal columns.** If `G` is a `k × m` standard Gaussian
matrix and `U` (`m × d`) has orthonormal columns (`Uᵀ U = 1`), then `G U` is a `k × d` standard
Gaussian matrix.

HMT 2011, §10.1–10.2 (rotational invariance applied on the right). Atlas: `rotation-invariance`
(corollary; audit G2 C10). Proof: `G U = (Uᵀ Gᵀ)ᵀ`, `gaussianMatrix_map_transpose` and the block
law `gaussianMatrix_map_block`. The orthonormality hypothesis is `HasOrthonormalCols U`
unfolded.
atlas: gaussian-matrix-mulvec-law

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_orthogonal {p m : ℕ} (U : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ) (V : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ)
  (hU : U.transpose * U = 1) (hV : V.transpose * V = 1) :
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => Matrix.of.symm (U * Matrix.of G * V)) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m) =
    NLAlib.gaussianMatrix p m
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_orthogonal
doc:
**Orthogonal invariance of the standard Gaussian matrix.** For orthogonal `U` (`p × p`) and
`V` (`m × m`), the law of `U G V` is the law of `G` when `G` is a `p × m` standard Gaussian
matrix.

HMT 2011 (Halko–Martinsson–Tropp), §10.1 (rotational invariance of the standard Gaussian
matrix). Atlas: `rotation-invariance`. The law is the pushforward of
`gaussianMatrix p m` (a measure on `Fin p → Fin m → ℝ`), so the map is written with
`Matrix.of.symm`. Ported from the Prove2me workspace, Gaussian Random Matrices series.
atlas: rotation-invariance

signature:
NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_Ioc_le_of_antitone_density {r k : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hrk : r ≤ k)
  (h : ℝ → ℝ) (hh : Measurable h) (hnn : ∀ y ∈ Set.Ioi 0, 0 ≤ h y) (hanti : AntitoneOn h (Set.Ioi 0))
  (hdens :
    (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2)
            (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k)).restrict
        (Set.Ioi 0) =
      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Ioi 0)).withDensity fun y =>
        ENNReal.ofReal (y ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.exp (-y / 2) * h y))
  (t : ℝ) :
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun G => NLAlib.sigmaMin (Matrix.of G).transpose ^ 2) (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix r k))
      (Set.Ioc 0 t) ≤
    ∫⁻ (y : ℝ) in Set.Ioc 0 t,
      ENNReal.ofReal
        (2 ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) * Real.Gamma ((↑k + 1) / 2) / (Real.Gamma (↑r / 2) * Real.Gamma (↑k - ↑r + 1)) *
            y ^ ((↑k - ↑r - 1) / 2) *
          Real.exp (-y / 2))
name: NLAlib.gaussianMatrix_map_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_Ioc_le_of_antitone_density

  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :

matrices with `λmax ≤ L`, `𝔼 λmax(Y) ≤ √(2 v log d) + L log d / 3` and `P{λmax(Y) ≥ t} ≤
bernsteinTail d v L t`.

Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 6*.
atlas: matrix-bernstein

Tropp–Webber 2023, Thm 5.1 specialised to Nyström; Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §19.2): if
`A = FᵀF` and `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix with `t ≥ k + 2`, then
`tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩)` is integrable and
`E tr(A − A⟨Ω⟩) ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) · ‖F − ⟦F⟧ₖ‖_F²`.

then the Gaussian RSVD bound for `F`
(`integrable_and_integral_frobSq_residual_gaussianRangeFrame_le_bestRankFrobSq`).

`∑_{i>k} λᵢ(A) = ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_*` (the atlas form), an identification not formalized here.

`nystrom-structural`, `rsvd-expected-error`, `leverage-scores`).
atlas: nystrom-randomized

  {G : Ω → n → κ → ℝ} (hS : AEMeasurable S μ) (hG : AEMeasurable G μ) (hSG : ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun S G μ)

doc:
**Hutch++ is unbiased.** Let the deflation basis `Q(S)` be a function of a random sketch `S`
with `Q(s)ᵀQ(s) = I` for every `s`, and let the Hutchinson test matrix `G` be independent of `S`

`𝔼[tr(QᵀAQ) + tr_m((I − QQᵀ)A(I − QQᵀ))] = tr A`.

Atlas: `hutchpp-unbiased`; uses `hutchinson-unbiased`, `gaussian-conditioning`.

bounded `A`); `S` lives in an arbitrary measurable space.

            ((G.submatrix i.succAbove id).mulVec (G i)))⁻¹
name: NLAlib.inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self
doc:
**Diagonal entry of the inverse Gram matrix (Schur complement).** Let `G` have rows indexed by
`Fin (n + 1)`, let `H` be `G` with row `i` removed and `g = G i`. If `H Hᵀ` is invertible, then
`(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ = (‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g))⁻¹`, the inverse squared distance from `g` to the
row space of `H`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 / HMT 2011, Prop A.5 (proof of `E (G Gᵀ)⁻¹`).
Atlas: `inverse-wishart-mean` (helper). Proof ported from the Prove2me solution
`Sol_GaussianMatrix_schur_diag_inv` (adjugate computation).

    -(G.submatrix i.succAbove id * (G.submatrix i.succAbove id).transpose)⁻¹.mulVec
          ((G.submatrix i.succAbove id).mulVec (G i)) a *
      (G * G.transpose)⁻¹ i i

doc:
**Off-diagonal entry of the inverse Gram matrix (Schur complement).** Let `G` have rows
indexed by `Fin (n + 1)`, let `H` be `G` with row `i` removed and `g = G i`. If `H Hᵀ` is
invertible, then for every `a`, `(G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢ,ₛ₍ₐ₎ = -cₐ (G Gᵀ)⁻¹ᵢᵢ` with `s = i.succAbove` and
`c = (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ H g` the least-squares coefficients of `g` on the rows of `H`.

Helper for Tropp–Webber 2023, Lemma B.2 (second moments of the inverse Wishart matrix);
companion of `inv_self_mul_transpose_apply_self`. Atlas: `inverse-wishart-frob-moment`
(helper). Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.schur_offdiag_inv` (adjugate
computation).

signature:
NLAlib.isCGIterate_iff.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {c x₀ : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ}

  NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x ↔
    x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q ∧
      ∀ y ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q, NLAlib.cgObjective A c x ≤ NLAlib.cgObjective A c (x₀ + y)
name: NLAlib.isCGIterate_iff
doc:

signature:
NLAlib.isCGIterate_iff_isAffineMinimiser_quadForm_sub.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} :
  NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x ↔
    NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser (fun y => NLAlib.quadForm A (y - xs)) x₀ (NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) x
name: NLAlib.isCGIterate_iff_isAffineMinimiser_quadForm_sub
doc:
**CG minimises the `A`-norm error.** For symmetric `A` with `A x⋆ = c`, `x` is a `q`-th CG
iterate iff it minimises `‖· − x⋆‖_A² = quadForm A (· − x⋆)` over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.2.

name: NLAlib.isCGIterate_of_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero
doc:
**Galerkin orthogonality implies the CG minimality.** For symmetric positive semidefinite
`A`, if `x − x₀ ∈ K_q` and the residual `c − A x` is orthogonal to `K_q`, then `x` is a `q`-th CG
iterate. Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.1–38.2; Saad (2003), Prop. 5.2
(Petrov–Galerkin with `L = K`). Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

signature:

name: NLAlib.isCGLSIterate_iff_isCGIterate
doc:
**CGLS is CG on the normal equations.** `x` is a CGLS iterate for `min ‖b − Ax‖` iff it is
a CG iterate for `AᵀA x = Aᵀb` (same starting point, same Krylov space). Source: Saad (2003)
[`saad03`], §8.3 (CGNR).
atlas: cgls-lsqr-bound (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} :

    x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q ∧
      ∀ z ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q, A.mulVec z ⬝ᵥ (c - A.mulVec x) = 0
name: NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_forall_dotProduct_eq_zero
doc:
**Petrov–Galerkin characterisation.** `x` is a GMRES iterate iff `x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀)` and
the residual is orthogonal to `A K_q(A, r₀)`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 5.3 and

atlas: gmres-def (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_isAffineMinimiser.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) :
  NLAlib.IsGMRESIterate A c x₀ q x ↔
    NLAlib.IsAffineMinimiser (fun y => NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) (Polynomial.X ^ 2)) (y - xs)) x₀
      (NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q) x
name: NLAlib.isGMRESIterate_iff_isAffineMinimiser

doc:
The Chebyshev minimax theorem on `[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`: the least possible bound `M` for
`|p|` on `[a, b]` over polynomials `p` of degree at most `q` with `p(0) = 1` is
`1 / T_q((b + a)/(b − a))`, attained by `chebyshevResidual a b q`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], App.; Trefethen–Bau (1997), Thm 38.5;
Atlas: `chebyshev-minimax`.
atlas: chebyshev-minimax

signature:
NLAlib.isLeast_chebyshev_monic_minimax (q : ℕ) :
  IsLeast {M | ∃ p, p.Monic ∧ p.natDegree = q ∧ ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc (-1) 1, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M} (1 / 2 ^ (q - 1))

possible bound for `|p|` on `[−1, 1]` is `1 / 2^(q−1)`, attained by `2^(1−q) T_q`.
Source: Trefethen (2013), Thm 2.2 / Rivlin (1990), Cor. 2.1.1; Atlas: `chebyshev-monic-minimal`.
Deviation: stated for all `q`, including `q = 0` (where the value is `1`).

signature:
NLAlib.isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A P W : Matrix n n ℝ}

CG on `L⁻¹AL⁻ᵀ`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2.1 (split preconditioning).

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues_fintype.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {p : Type u_3}
  [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype p] [DecidableEq n] {S : Matrix p m ℝ} {U : Matrix m n ℝ}
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε ↔
    ∀ (j : Fin (Fintype.card n)),
      √(1 - ε) ≤ NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin p) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (S * U)) ↑j ∧
        NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin p) (Fintype.equivFin n)) (S * U)) ↑j ≤ √(1 + ε)
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_singularValues_fintype
doc:
Complete OSE singular-value criterion on arbitrary finite indices.
For `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`, every domain singular value of the normalized `S U` lies in
`[√(1−ε), √(1+ε)]` precisely when `S` embeds the frame's subspace.
Atlas `ose-def`, `svd`; the list uses explicit `Fin(card)` normalization.
atlas: ose-def

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_iff_specNorm_transpose_mul_self_sub_one_le
doc:
Complete Gram-form equivalence for an orthonormal frame, valid also in
empty dimensions. Atlas: `ose-def`.

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_mul_right_iff
doc:
Basis independence (Woodruff 2014 §2.1): for invertible `C`, `S` is an `ε`-subspace
embedding for `range U` iff it is one for `range (U C)`. The property depends on the subspace
only.

Atlas: `ose-def`.
atlas: ose-def

signature:
NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_forall_sqrt_le.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {k : Type u_1} {m : Type u_2} {d : Type u_3} [Fintype k]
  [Fintype m] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] {S : Matrix k m ℝ} {U : Matrix m d ℝ} (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U)
  {ε a : ℝ} (hε : ε ≤ 1) (ha : 0 ≤ a) (haε : 3 * a ≤ ε)
  (hlo : ∀ (x : d → ℝ), (1 - a) * √(x ⬝ᵥ x) ≤ √((S * U).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S * U).mulVec x))
  (hhi : ∀ (x : d → ℝ), √((S * U).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ (S * U).mulVec x) ≤ (1 + a) * √(x ⬝ᵥ x)) :
  NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε
name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_forall_sqrt_le
doc:
**Deterministic embedding criterion.** If `U` has orthonormal columns and every
`‖SUx‖` lies between `(1 − a)‖x‖` and `(1 + a)‖x‖`, with `0 ≤ a`, `3a ≤ ε ≤ 1`, then `S` is an
`ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` (since `(1 − a)² ≥ 1 − ε` and `(1 + a)² ≤ 1 + ε`).
Woodruff 2014, proof of Thm 2.3; atlas `gaussian-ose` (helper; uses `ose-def`).
atlas: gaussian-ose

name: NLAlib.isSubspaceEmbedding_of_specNorm_transpose_mul_self_sub_one_le

direction used in practice: for `U` with orthonormal columns, `‖(SU)ᵀ(SU) − I‖₂ ≤ ε` implies
that `S` is an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U`. (The converse also holds; not yet
formalized.)

Atlas: `ose-def`.

signature:
NLAlib.isometry_reflection_identities.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ]
  [DecidableEq κ] (K : Matrix ι κ ℂ) (hK : K.conjTranspose * K = 1) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (B : Matrix κ κ ℂ) :
  have U := Matrix.fromBlocks (1 - K * K.conjTranspose) K K.conjTranspose 0;
  U.IsHermitian ∧ U * U = 1 ∧ (U * Matrix.fromBlocks A 0 0 B * U).toBlocks₂₂ = K.conjTranspose * A * K

doc:

Tropp 2015, proof of Thm 8.5.2 (unitary dilation). Atlas: `operator-monotone-convex`. Ported from
the Prove2me mission *An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 8*.

Auxiliary; not a numbered result in the source.

signature: NLAlib.jacobiFraction (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction
doc:
The finite Jacobi (Stieltjes) continued fraction with `m` levels starting at level `k`:
`jacobiFraction a β x 0 k = 0` and
`jacobiFraction a β x (m+1) k = 1 / (x − a k − β (k+1)² · jacobiFraction a β x m (k+1))`, so
`jacobiFraction a β x m 0 = 1/(x − a₀ − β₁²/(x − a₁ − ⋯ − β_{m−1}²/(x − a_{m−1})))`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3. Atlas: `jacobi-matrix-identities`.

signature:
NLAlib.jacobiFraction.eq_def (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (x✝ x✝¹ : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.jacobiFraction a β x x✝ x✝¹ =
    match x✝, x✝¹ with
    | 0, x => 0
    | m.succ, k => 1 / (x - a k - β (k + 1) ^ 2 * NLAlib.jacobiFraction a β x m (k + 1))
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction.eq_def

signature:
NLAlib.jacobiFraction_succ (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (m k : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.jacobiFraction a β x m (k + 1) = NLAlib.jacobiFraction (fun i => a (i + 1)) (fun i => β (i + 1)) x m k
name: NLAlib.jacobiFraction_succ
doc: Shifting the start level of a Jacobi fraction shifts the coefficients.

signature: NLAlib.jacobiMatrix (a β : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ
name: NLAlib.jacobiMatrix
doc:
The symmetric tridiagonal (Jacobi) matrix with diagonal `a 0, …, a (m−1)` and
off-diagonal entries `(i, i+1)`, `(i+1, i)` equal to `β (i+1)`.
Source: Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 3. Atlas: `jacobi-matrix-identities`.

signature:
NLAlib.jl_distributional (k n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G | |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec x - x ⬝ᵥ x| > ε * x ⬝ᵥ x} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_distributional
doc:
**Distributional Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma** for the Gaussian sketch: for
`S = k^{-1/2} G` with `G` standard Gaussian `k × n`, any fixed `x : ℝⁿ` and `0 < ε < 1`,
`P[|‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²| > ε‖x‖²] ≤ 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Lem 2.2 (stated there for the projection of a random unit vector; the
Gaussian-sketch form is Woodruff 2014 §2.1). Atlas: `jl-distributional`; uses
`gaussian-matrix-mulVec-law`, `chi-square-upper-tail`, `chi-square-lower-tail`.

Proof: with `u = x/‖x‖`, `‖Sx‖² = (‖x‖²/k) ‖Gu‖²` and `Gu` is a standard Gaussian vector, so the
event lies in `{χ²_k ≥ (1+ε)k} ∪ {χ²_k ≤ (1−ε)k}`. The Chernoff tails and
`log(1+ε) ≤ ε − ε²/2 + ε³/3`, `log(1−ε) ≤ −ε − ε²/2` bound each part by `exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.
Degenerate cases: for `x = 0` the event is empty; for `k = 0` the bound is `2`.
atlas: jl-distributional

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (↑N ^ 2 * 2 * Real.exp (-↑k * (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)))
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, union-bound form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for a finite
family `p : Fin N → ℝⁿ`, the probability that the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` distorts some
pairwise squared distance `‖p i − p j‖²` by more than a factor `1 ± ε` is at most
`N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6))`.

Deviation: the union is taken over all `N²` ordered pairs (not the `N(N−1)/2` unordered ones),
which costs a constant factor `2` in the bound. No measurability hypothesis is needed (the union
bound holds for the outer measure).

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  ∃ S,
    ∀ (i j : Fin N),
      (1 - ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j) ≤ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ∧
        S.mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ S.mulVec (p i - p j) ≤ (1 + ε) * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_exists
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, existence form (Johnson–Lindenstrauss 1984; Dasgupta–Gupta
2003, Thm 2.1): any `N ≥ 2` points of `ℝⁿ` admit a linear map `S : ℝⁿ → ℝᵏ` with
`k ≥ 48 log N / ε²` that preserves every pairwise squared distance to within `1 ± ε`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hN : 2 ≤ N)
  (hk : 48 * Real.log ↑N / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2)
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_half
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, `O(ε⁻² log N)` form (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): for
`N ≥ 2` points, `0 < ε < 1` and `k ≥ 48 log N / ε²`, the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G`
distorts some pairwise squared distance by more than `1 ± ε` with probability at most `1/2`.

Deviation: the explicit constant `48` (from `(ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ ≤ 12/ε²` and
`log(4N²) ≤ 4 log N` for `N ≥ 2`) is not optimised; Dasgupta–Gupta's constant is `4·(1/2 − ε/3)⁻¹`
at failure probability `1 − 1/N`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

signature:
NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le (k n N : ℕ) (p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hk : (ε ^ 2 / 4 - ε ^ 3 / 6)⁻¹ * Real.log (2 * ↑N ^ 2 / δ) ≤ ↑k) :
  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k n)
      {G |
        ∃ i j,
          i ≠ j ∧
            |((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G).mulVec (p i - p j) -
                  (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)| >
              ε * (p i - p j) ⬝ᵥ (p i - p j)} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal δ
name: NLAlib.jl_lemma_prob_le_of_log_le
doc:
Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma with explicit dimension (Dasgupta–Gupta 2003, Thm 2.1): if
`0 < ε < 1`, `0 < δ` and `k ≥ (ε²/4 − ε³/6)⁻¹ log(2N²/δ)`, then with probability at least
`1 − δ` the Gaussian sketch `S = k^{-1/2} G` preserves all pairwise squared distances of
`p : Fin N → ℝⁿ` to within `1 ± ε`.

Deviation: Dasgupta–Gupta take `k ≥ 4 (ε²/2 − ε³/3)⁻¹ log N`, aiming at success probability
`1/N`; we state the general-`δ` form with the constant coming from the ordered-pair union bound
in `jl_lemma`.

Atlas: `jl-lemma`; uses `jl-distributional`.
atlas: jl-lemma

NLAlib.kaczmarzRowPathPMF.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

The exact distribution of an independent sequence of row choices.

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k] [DecidableEq k]
  (Q : Matrix n k ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) : n → ℝ
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox
doc:
The Krylov (Lanczos-FA) approximation of `f(A) b` from a basis matrix `Q`:
`Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b`, with `f(QᵀAQ) = cfc f (Qᵀ * A * Q)`. With the Lanczos basis, `Qᵀ b = ‖b‖ e₁`
and this is `‖b‖ Q f(T_q) e₁`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], eq. (3.2); Higham (2008)
[`higham08`], §13.2. Deviation: any `Q` (the theorems assume orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`). Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (definition).

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_congr.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {k' : Type u_3} [Fintype k'] [DecidableEq k']
  {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} {Q' : Matrix n k' ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q) (hQ' : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q')
  (hR : Q.mulVecLin.range = Q'.mulVecLin.range) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A f b = NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q' A f b
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_congr
doc:
**Lanczos-FA depends only on the range of `Q`.** If `Q` and `Q'` have orthonormal columns
and the same range, then `Q f(QᵀAQ) Qᵀ b = Q' f(Q'ᵀAQ') Q'ᵀ b` (for `Q' = QU` with `U`
orthogonal, `f(UᵀTU) = Uᵀ f(T) U`). Source: `docs/KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS.md` §3.9; Saad (1992)
[`saad92`], §3 (basis-independence of the Krylov projection).
Deviation: `A` symmetric (for nonsymmetric `A` the real `cfc` is not the matrix function).
Atlas: `lanczos-fa-error` (helper: basis independence of the approximant).

name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eq_aeval_interpolate
doc:
**Lanczos-FA is the interpolant at the Ritz values.** If `Q` has at most `q` columns, then
`krylovFunApprox Q A f b = p(A) b` for the Lagrange interpolant `p` of `f` at the distinct
eigenvalues of `QᵀAQ`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.3.
Deviation: `Q` is any orthonormal matrix with at most `q` columns and `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q` (the
source takes the Lanczos basis, `range Q = K_q`); the Ritz values are interpolated without
multiplicity (Lagrange, not Hermite), which suffices because `f(T)` only sees `f` on `spec T`.
Atlas: proposed id `lanczos-fa-interpolation`; uses `krylov-polynomial-exactness`.
atlas: lanczos-fa-interpolation

name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eq_aeval_of_forall_eval_eq
doc:
**Lanczos-FA interpolates at the Ritz values (general form).** If `p` has `deg p < q` and
agrees with `f` at the eigenvalues of `T = QᵀAQ` (the Ritz values), then
`krylovFunApprox Q A f b = p(A) b`. Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Thm 3.3.
Deviation: any orthonormal `Q` with `K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`; Lagrange (not Hermite)
interpolation, the agreement being only required at the Ritz values.
Atlas: proposed id `lanczos-fa-interpolation`; uses `krylov-polynomial-exactness`.
atlas: lanczos-fa-interpolation

signature:
NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eval_eq_aeval.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {k : Type u_2} [Fintype k]
  [DecidableEq k] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian) {Q : Matrix n k ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  (b : n → ℝ) {q : ℕ} (hK : NLAlib.krylovSpace A b q ≤ Q.mulVecLin.range) {p : Polynomial ℝ} (hp : p.degree < ↑q) :
  NLAlib.krylovFunApprox Q A (fun x => Polynomial.eval x p) b = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec b
name: NLAlib.krylovFunApprox_eval_eq_aeval
doc:
**Lanczos-FA is exact on polynomials.** For symmetric `A`, `Q` with orthonormal columns and
`K_q(A,b) ⊆ range Q`, `krylovFunApprox Q A p b = p(A) b` for every `p` with `deg p < q`.
Source: Saad (1992) [`saad92`], Lemma 3.1.
Deviation: the matrix-function form needs `A` symmetric (so that `QᵀAQ` is self-adjoint and
`cfc` is the polynomial calculus); `mulVec_aeval_transpose_mul_mul_mulVec_eq` is the form for
any `A`.
atlas: krylov-polynomial-exactness (partial)

signature: NLAlib.krylovGrade.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) : ℕ

name: NLAlib.leverageScore
doc:
The **leverage score** of row `i` of `A`: `ℓᵢ(A) = (A A⁺)ᵢᵢ`, the `i`-th diagonal entry of
the orthogonal projector onto `range A`. Defined for every real matrix (any rank, empty
shapes). Drineas–Mahoney–Muthukrishnan–Woodruff 2012, Def. 1; Woodruff 2014, Def. 2.12.
Atlas `leverage-scores`.
atlas: leverage-scores

name: NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_hasOrthonormalCols
doc:
**Leverage scores are squared row norms of any orthonormal basis.** If `U` has
orthonormal columns and is a basis of `range A` (`range A ⊆ range U`, written `U (Uᵀ A) = A`,
and `U` has at most `rank A` columns), then `ℓᵢ(A) = ∑ⱼ Uᵢⱼ² = ‖U_{i,:}‖²`. Since the left side
does not mention `U`, the row norms do not depend on the choice of basis.
Drineas–Mahoney–Muthukrishnan–Woodruff 2012, Def. 1 and the remark after it; Woodruff 2014,
Def. 2.12. Atlas `leverage-scores`. Deviation: "orthonormal basis of `range A`" is spelled as the
two hypotheses `hUA`, `hr` (together with orthonormality they force `range U = range A`).
atlas: leverage-scores

signature:

  NLAlib.leverageScore U i = ∑ j, U i j ^ 2
name: NLAlib.leverageScore_eq_sum_sq_of_self
doc:
For a matrix `U` with orthonormal columns, `ℓᵢ(U) = ∑ⱼ Uᵢⱼ²`.
Woodruff 2014, §2.4; atlas `leverage-scores`.

`S` (entrywise measurable) satisfies `E (‖Sx‖² − ‖x‖²)² ≤ ε² ‖x‖⁴` for every `x`, with `ε ≥ 0`,
then for fixed `A ∈ ℝ^{n×d₁}`, `B ∈ ℝ^{n×d₂}`,
`E ‖AᵀSᵀSB − AᵀB‖_F² ≤ ε² ‖A‖_F² ‖B‖_F²`.

Woodruff 2014, Thm 2.8 (the `ℓ = 2` case of the `(ε, δ, ℓ)`-JL moment property; Kane–Nelson
2014); Sarlós 2006, Lem 6. Atlas `amm-ose`. Deviations: stated with lower Lebesgue integrals
(no integrability hypothesis); the hypothesis is the second-moment property itself, not a tail
bound; constant `1`.
atlas: amm-ose

name: NLAlib.matrixMeasurableSpace
doc:
The Borel σ-algebra on complex matrices (for the norm topology), used to state measurability of
random matrices.

This global instance is a deliberate exception to STANDARDS §3, which states measurability of
matrix-valued maps entrywise because Mathlib has no `MeasurableSpace (Matrix m n ℂ)`. The matrix
concentration development (ported from the Tropp 2015 Prove2me missions) treats random matrices as
`Measurable` maps into a normed space and integrates them as Bochner integrals in the operator
norm; every statement in `NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/` that mentions `Measurable`, `iIndepFun` or
`Integrable` for a matrix-valued map elaborates through this instance, so removing it would mean
restating the whole development. Mathlib declares no competing instance (`Matrix` is a
non-reducible `def`, so the product σ-algebra on `m → n → ℂ` is not found), hence no diamond. It
could be made `scoped`: checked 2026-10-09, wrapping it in `namespace MatrixBorel` as a `scoped
instance` and adding `open scoped NLAlib.MatrixBorel` to the 35 modules under
`Concentration/Matrix/` that import this one (directly or not) builds cleanly, at the price of
every downstream user opening the scope to state the hypotheses of the public theorems.

signature:

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d N : ℕ} [NeZero d] (X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (L : ℝ)
  (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hMeas : ∀ (k : Fin N), Measurable (X k)) (hIndep : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X μ)
  (hHerm : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, (X k ω).IsHermitian)
  (hBound : ∀ (k : Fin N), ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂μ, 0 ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMin (X k ω) ∧ NLAlib.lambdaMax (X k ω) ≤ L) :
  have Y := fun ω => ∑ k, X k ω;
  have a := NLAlib.lambdaMin (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  have b := NLAlib.lambdaMax (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ∂μ);
  a = NLAlib.lambdaMin (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
    b = NLAlib.lambdaMax (∑ k, ∫ (ω : Ω), X k ω ∂μ) ∧
      (∀ (θ : ℝ),
          0 < θ →
            (1 - Real.exp (-θ)) / θ * a - L * Real.log ↑d / θ ≤ ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ∂μ ∧
              ∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω) ∂μ ≤ (Real.exp θ - 1) / θ * b + L * Real.log ↑d / θ) ∧
        (∀ (ε : ℝ),
            0 ≤ ε → ε < 1 → (μ {ω | NLAlib.lambdaMin (Y ω) ≤ (1 - ε) * a}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffLowerTail d a L ε) ∧
          ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε → (μ {ω | (1 + ε) * b ≤ NLAlib.lambdaMax (Y ω)}).toReal ≤ NLAlib.chernoffUpperTail d b L ε

doc:
Matrix Chernoff inequality: for an independent sum of random positive semidefinite matrices with
`λmax ≤ L`, expectation bounds on `λmin` and `λmax` for every `θ > 0` and the lower and upper
tails `chernoffLowerTail`, `chernoffUpperTail`.

Tropp 2015, Thm 5.1.1, eqs (5.1.1–6). Atlas: `matrix-chernoff`. Ported from the Prove2me mission
*An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 5*.

The expectation bounds are stated for every `θ > 0` before optimisation; degenerate `L = 0`
follows the piecewise tail definitions.

matrix are independent and sub-Gaussian with variance proxy `K²`, then for `m = |κ| ≥ 1` and

`P(|tr_m(A) − 𝔼 tr_m(A)| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp(−(1/(256e²)) min(m t²/(K⁴‖A‖_F²), m t/(K²‖A‖)))`.

`hanson-wright`. Deviation: Hanson–Wright constant `1/(256 e²)`; any matrix `A` (not only
symmetric); the centring is the true mean (equal to `tr A` for isotropic entries, see the
Gaussian and Rademacher corollaries).

(2021) [`mmmw21`], Lem. 2. Atlas: `hutchinson-tail`; uses `hanson-wright`,
`hutchinson-unbiased`. Deviation: constant `1/(256 e²)`.

with `tr A > 0`, `0 < ε ≤ 1`, `0 < δ`, and `m ≥ 256 e² ε⁻² log(2/δ)`, then
`P(|tr_m(A) − tr A| ≥ ε tr A) ≤ δ`.

Meyer–Musco–Musco–Woodruff (2021) [`mmmw21`], Lem. 2. Atlas: `hutchinson-tail`.
Deviation: constant `256 e²`.

doc:
**Small-ball estimate for the smallest singular value of a Gaussian matrix.** For an
`N × n` standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `1 ≤ n ≤ N` and `n s² ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(σ_min(A) ≤ s) ≤ n · (e n s² / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`. The source's hypothesis
`0 ≤ s` is not needed and is dropped.

Rudelson–Vershynin 2009 (sharper `(C s √N)^{N-n+1}` form). Union bound over the columns of the
column-distance estimate. Atlas: `smin-small-ball`. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.sMin_small_ball`.
