signature:
NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal {N p d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
  (hrank : B.rank + d ≤ N) (u : ℝ) (hu : 0 ≤ u) (hud : u ≤ ↑d) :
  (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)
      {g | (⨅ c, √((g - B.mulVec c) ⬝ᵥ (g - B.mulVec c))) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤
    ENNReal.ofReal ((Real.exp 1 * u / ↑d) ^ (↑d / 2))
name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_colSpace_le_le_gaussianReal
doc:
**Small ball for the distance to a subspace.** Let `B : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin p) ℝ` have
`rank B + d ≤ N` with `d ≥ 1`. For a standard Gaussian vector `g ∈ ℝᴺ` and `0 ≤ u ≤ d`,
`P(dist(g, range B)² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / d)^{d/2}`, with `dist(g, range B) = inf_c ‖g - B c‖₂`.

The squared distance dominates the sum of squares of `d` coordinates of `g` in an orthonormal
basis of `(range B)ᗮ` (Bessel), which is `χ²_d` by rotation invariance; then the chi-square lower
tail. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.gaussian_dist_colspace_small_ball`.
atlas: smin-small-ball

  (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix N n) {A | (⨅ x, √((Matrix.of A).mulVec ↑x ⬝ᵥ (Matrix.of A).mulVec ↑x)) ^ 2 ≤ u} ≤

name: NLAlib.measure_sq_dist_col_span_le_le_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Small ball for the distance from a column to the span of the others.** For an `N × n`
standard Gaussian matrix `A` with `n ≤ N`, any column `j` and `0 ≤ u ≤ N - n + 1`,
`P(dist(A_j, span{A_l : l ≠ j})² ≤ u) ≤ (e u / (N - n + 1))^{(N - n + 1)/2}`, the distance
being written `inf { ‖A x‖₂ : x_j = 1 }`.

Condition on the other columns (resample column `j`) and apply the subspace small-ball bound
with `d = N - n + 1`. Davidson–Szarek 2001, proof of Thm II.13; Vershynin 2012, §5.2.
Atlas: `smin-small-ball` (step). Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.dist_col_span_small_ball`.
atlas: smin-small-ball

  [Fintype n] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq q] {Q : Matrix m q ℝ} (hQ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols Q)
  {Y : Matrix m n ℝ} (hQY : Q * (Q.transpose * Y) = Y) (hr : Fintype.card q ≤ Y.rank) :
  Q * Q.transpose = Y * NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse Y
name: NLAlib.mul_transpose_eq_mul_moorePenroseInverse
doc:
**Uniqueness of the orthogonal projector onto a range.** If `Q` has orthonormal columns,
`range Y ⊆ range Q` (written `Q (Qᵀ Y) = Y`) and `rank Y` is at least the number of columns of
`Q` (so the two ranges coincide), then `QQᵀ = Y Y⁺`.

Proof: `P₁ = QQᵀ` and `P₂ = YY⁺` are symmetric idempotents with `P₁P₂ = P₂ = P₂P₁`, so
`M = P₁ − P₂` is a symmetric idempotent and `‖M‖_F² = tr M = card q − rank Y ≤ 0`.
Standard (Golub–Van Loan, 4th ed., §2.5.1: the orthogonal projector onto a subspace is unique).
Atlas `leverage-scores` (basis independence), `projection-facts`. Belongs in
`Matrix/MoorePenrose.lean`.

signature:
NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_limit_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ρ w : ι → ℝ)
  (i₀ : ι) (hρ₀ : ρ i₀ = 1) (hρ : ∀ (i : ι), i ≠ i₀ → 0 ≤ ρ i ∧ ρ i < 1) (b₀ k : ℝ) (hb₀ : 0 ≤ b₀) (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w i₀)
  (hrel : ∀ (j : ι), j ≠ i₀ → b₀ * ρ j * (w j - w i₀) = 1 - ρ j) :
  (2 * k -
      2 * b₀ *
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j,
            if i = j then 0
            else w j * ρ i * ρ j * (((if j = i₀ then 1 else 0) - if i = i₀ then 1 else 0) / (ρ j - ρ i))) ≤
    2 * (k - ↑(Fintype.card ι) + 1)
name: NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_limit_le
doc:
The limiting Gram Laplacian is at most the hard-edge coefficient
`2(k-r+1)`. Source: operator soft minimum gap correction; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sharp limiting coefficient helper).
The algebraic ratio identity holds for `ρj=(λmin+ε)/(λj+ε)` and
`b₀=1/(λmin+ε)`, with `w` the Gram eigenvalues.

signature:
NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_symmetric_limit_le.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  (ρ w : ι → ℝ) (i₀ : ι) (hρ₀ : ρ i₀ = 1) (hρ : ∀ (i : ι), i ≠ i₀ → 0 ≤ ρ i ∧ ρ i < 1) (b₀ k : ℝ) (hb₀ : 0 ≤ b₀)
  (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w i₀) (hrel : ∀ (j : ι), j ≠ i₀ → b₀ * ρ j * (w j - w i₀) = 1 - ρ j) :
  2 * k -
      b₀ *
        ∑ i,
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i,
            (w i + w j) * ρ i * ρ j * (((if j = i₀ then 1 else 0) - if i = i₀ then 1 else 0) / (ρ j - ρ i)) ≤

name: NLAlib.normalized_inverse_power_laplacian_symmetric_limit_le
doc:
The symmetric limiting Gram Laplacian is bounded by the exact
hard-edge coefficient. Source: inverse spectral gap correction; atlas
`wishart-lambda-min-tail` (sharp limiting bound helper).

signature:
NLAlib.one_sub_le_measure_isSubspaceEmbedding_gaussianMatrix {k m d : ℕ} (U : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin d) ℝ)
  (hU : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U) {ε δ : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) (hδ0 : 0 < δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1)
  (hk : 18 * (↑d + 2 * Real.log (2 / δ)) / ε ^ 2 ≤ ↑k) :
  1 - ENNReal.ofReal δ ≤ (NLAlib.gaussianMatrix k m) {G | NLAlib.IsSubspaceEmbedding ((1 / √↑k) • Matrix.of G) U ε}
name: NLAlib.one_sub_le_measure_isSubspaceEmbedding_gaussianMatrix
doc:
**Gaussian oblivious subspace embedding.** Let `U ∈ ℝ^{m×d}` have orthonormal columns,
`0 < ε ≤ 1`, `0 < δ ≤ 1` and `k ≥ 18 (d + 2 log(2/δ)) / ε²`. Then a `k × m` standard Gaussian
matrix `G` makes `S = k^{-1/2} G` an `ε`-subspace embedding for `range U` with probability at least
`1 − δ`.

Woodruff 2014, Thm 2.3 (stated there with unspecified constants); Martinsson–Tropp 2020, §8.7,
§9.3. Atlas `gaussian-ose` (uses `ose-def`, `extreme-singular-values-deviation`,
`rotation-invariance`). Deviations: explicit constant `18` and `2 log(2/δ)` in place of the
atlas's `C` and `log(1/δ)`; the probability is an outer-measure lower bound (no measurability of
the embedding event is claimed); `d = 0` holds trivially.
atlas: gaussian-ose

integral written out in the Prove2me statements. Source: Bakry–Gentil–Ledoux 2014, (2.7.1).

`GaussianMatrix.ou_entropy_hasDerivAt` (`ouP`) and

doc:

`H`, `‖g‖² - (H g)ᵀ (H Hᵀ)⁻¹ (H g)`, has the `χ²_{k-n}` law (the law of `∑ⱼ Xⱼ²`,
`X ~ N(0, I_{k-n})`).

(helper). Proof ported from the Prove2me solution `Sol_GaussianMatrix_residual_law`

  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (g p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i,
      Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) g * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 *
        ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ g(λᵢ) p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A` and polynomials
`p`, `g`. Atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {g p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hg : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ Polynomial.eval x g) (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤
    M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm ((Polynomial.aeval A) g) v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, weighted form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S`, the weight polynomial `g` is nonnegative on `S` and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ g(A) (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ g(A) v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_{g(A)} ≤ M ‖v‖_{g(A)}`. The weights
`g = X` (energy norm, CG), `g = X²` (residual norm, MINRES) and `g = 1` (error norm) are the
cases used by Krylov methods. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1; Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29 (case `g = X`). Generalises `quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le` (KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2).
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (p : Polynomial ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) =
    ∑ i, hA.eigenvalues i * Polynomial.eval (hA.eigenvalues i) p ^ 2 * ((hA.eigenvectorBasis i).ofLp ⬝ᵥ v) ^ 2
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_eq_sum
doc:
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ p(λᵢ)² ⟨uᵢ, v⟩²` for real symmetric `A`. Audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  {p : Polynomial ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} {M : ℝ} (hS : S ⊆ Set.Ici 0) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ S)
  (hp : ∀ x ∈ S, |Polynomial.eval x p| ≤ M) (v : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec v) ≤ M ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A v
name: NLAlib.quadForm_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Polynomial bound, energy form.** If every eigenvalue of the real symmetric `A` lies in
`S ⊆ [0, ∞)` (so `A` is positive semidefinite) and `|p| ≤ M` on `S`, then
`(p(A)v)ᵀ A (p(A)v) ≤ M² vᵀ A v`, i.e. `‖p(A) v‖_A ≤ M ‖v‖_A`. This is the form used for the
CG error (Greenbaum 1997, §3.1; Saad 2003, Thm 6.29); audit G3 C1;
atlas `polynomial-spectral-bound`. The case `g = X` of `quadForm_aeval_aeval_mulVec_le`.
atlas: polynomial-spectral-bound

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.chebyshevIterate a b A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_chebyshevIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Chebyshev iteration, `A`-norm rate.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
`0 < a < b`, and `A x⋆ = c`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.3; Golub–Varga (1961) [`gv61`]. Deviation: squared norms;
the iterate is defined by its residual polynomial (no recurrence).
atlas: chebyshev-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A z = ∑ i, ∑ j, A i j * (z i * z j)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum
doc: Expansion `zᵀ A z = ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ A_ij z_i z_j`. Atlas: `hutchinson-unbiased` (helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_eigenvalues

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_hutchinsonBlock.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
  (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (Z : n → κ → ℝ) :
  (NLAlib.quadForm (NLAlib.hutchinsonBlock κ A) fun e => Z e.1 e.2) = NLAlib.hutchinsonEstimate A Z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_hutchinsonBlock
doc:
The quadratic form of the block matrix at `vec(Z)` is the Hutchinson estimator.
Atlas: `hutchinson-tail` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_nonneg_of_eigenvalues_nonneg.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hpsd : ∀ (i : n), 0 ≤ hA.eigenvalues i) (x : n → ℝ) : 0 ≤ NLAlib.quadForm A x
name: NLAlib.quadForm_nonneg_of_eigenvalues_nonneg
doc:
A symmetric matrix with nonnegative eigenvalues has `xᵀ A x ≥ 0`. Moved from
`Krylov/CG.lean` (atlas `cg-convergence`, helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_polyIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Error bound for a polynomial method, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in
`S`, a weight `g ≥ 0` on `S` and `|1 − x s(x)| ≤ M` on `S`,
`‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`. Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §12.1;
Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_reindex.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (e : ι ≃ κ)
  (z : ι → ℝ) : (NLAlib.quadForm ((Matrix.reindex e e) A) fun k => z (e.symm k)) = NLAlib.quadForm A z
name: NLAlib.quadForm_reindex
doc:
Relabelling the coordinates by an equivalence does not change the quadratic form.
Atlas `hanson-wright` (index transport).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le
doc:
**Richardson contraction, weighted norm.** For symmetric `A` with spectrum in `[a, b]`,
step `ω ≥ 0`, `A x⋆ = c` and a weight `g ≥ 0` on `[a, b]`,
`‖x_q − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ ρ^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}` with `ρ = max(|1 − ωa|, |1 − ωb|)`. With
`g = X` (`0 ≤ a`) this is the `A`-norm bound of the atlas, with `g = 1` the Euclidean error.
Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1; Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c xs : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) (x₀ : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (NLAlib.richardsonIterate (2 / (a + b)) A c x₀ q - xs) ≤
    (((b - a) / (b + a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_richardsonIterate_sub_le_of_optimal
doc:
**Richardson with the optimal step** `ω = 2/(a + b)`: for symmetric positive definite `A`
with spectrum in `[a, b]`, `0 < a ≤ b`, `‖x_q − x⋆‖²_A ≤ ((b − a)/(b + a))^{2q} ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_A`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §4.2.1; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §2.1.
Deviation: unpreconditioned (`P = I`), squared norms.
atlas: richardson-iteration (partial)

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_rowSelector.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (i : n) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm (NLAlib.rowSelector A i) z = z i * A.mulVec z i
name: NLAlib.quadForm_rowSelector
doc: `zᵀ (rowSelector A i) z = zᵢ (A z)ᵢ`. Atlas: `diagonal-estimator` (helper).

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sq_eq_sum.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (z : n → ℝ) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A z ^ 2 = ∑ i, ∑ j, ∑ k, ∑ l, A i j * A k l * (z i * z j * z k * z l)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sq_eq_sum
doc:
Expansion `(zᵀ A z)² = ∑ᵢⱼₖₗ A_ij A_kl z_i z_j z_k z_l`. Atlas: `hutchinson-variance`
(helper).

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimiser
doc:
**The class theorem.** Let `A` be symmetric, `A x⋆ = c`, and `g` a weight polynomial with
`g(λᵢ) ≥ 0` at every eigenvalue. If `x` minimises `‖· − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} = quadForm (g(A)) (· − x⋆)`
over `x₀ + K_q(A, r₀)`, then for every residual polynomial `p` (`deg p ≤ q`, `p(0) = 1`) with
`|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue, `‖x − x⋆‖²_{g(A)} ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖²_{g(A)}`.
CG is `g = X` (via `cgObjective_eq_add_quadForm_sub`), MINRES `g = X²`, the error-minimising
method `g = 1`. Source: Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], §3.1 (CG) and §3.2 (MINRES);
Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Thm 6.29; KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS §3.2.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`, `minres-bound` (the shared step; tags are on the instances).
atlas: affine-krylov-minimiser

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x - xs) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate
doc:
**CG convergence, condition-number form.** Let `A` be symmetric with every eigenvalue in
`[a, b]`, `0 < a < b`, `A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2 ((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`; with `κ = b/a`,
`(√b − √a)/(√b + √a) = (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1)`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.5; Golub–Meurant (2010) [`gm10`], Ch. 8.
Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `chebyshev-minimax`, `polynomial-spectral-bound`,
`krylov-subspace`. Deviation: squared `A`-norms (the source states the unsquared form).
atlas: cg-convergence

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : A.IsHermitian) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a ≤ b) (hspec : ∀ (i : n), hA.eigenvalues i ∈ Set.Icc a b)
  {c x₀ xs x : n → ℝ} (hxs : A.mulVec xs = c) {q : ℕ} (hx : NLAlib.IsCGIterate A c x₀ q x) :
  NLAlib.quadForm A (x - xs) ≤ (2 * ((√b - √a) / (√b + √a)) ^ q) ^ 2 * NLAlib.quadForm A (x₀ - xs)
name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le
doc:
**CG convergence, condition-number form including `a = b`.** As
`quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate` but for `0 < a ≤ b`. When `a = b` (`A = aI`), CG is exact
after one step and the bound reads `0` for `q ≥ 1` and `4 ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` for `q = 0`.
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.5. Atlas: `cg-convergence`.

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_poly
doc:
**CG error bound, polynomial form.** Let `A` be symmetric positive semidefinite,
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th CG iterate from `x₀`. For every polynomial `p` with `deg p ≤ q`,
`p(0) = 1` and `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` at every eigenvalue,
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ M² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²` (with `‖v‖_A² = quadForm A v`).
Source: Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Thm 38.3 (and the inequality (38.10)); Saad (2003),
Thm 6.29. Atlas: `cg-convergence`; uses `polynomial-spectral-bound`, `krylov-subspace`,
`residual-polynomial` (the case `g = X` of `quadForm_sub_le_of_isAffineMinimiser`).
atlas: cg-convergence

name: NLAlib.quadForm_sub_le_of_isPCGIterate
doc:
**Preconditioned CG bound under a Loewner sandwich.** Let `P` be positive definite, `A` with
`a P ≼ A ≼ b P` for `0 < a ≤ b` (so `A` is symmetric positive definite and `κ(P⁻¹A) ≤ b/a`),
`A x⋆ = c`, and `x` a `q`-th PCG iterate from `x₀`. Then
`‖x − x⋆‖_A² ≤ (2((√b − √a)/(√b + √a))^q)² ‖x₀ − x⋆‖_A²`.
Proof: CG on `P^{-1/2} A P^{-1/2}`, whose spectrum lies in `[a, b]`
(`isPCGIterate_iff_isCGIterate`, `quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate_of_le`).
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §9.2; Greenbaum (1997) [`greenbaum97`], Ch. 8.
Deviation: squared `A`-norms.
atlas: preconditioned-cg

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_transpose_mul_mul.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] (A W : Matrix n n ℝ) (v : n → ℝ) :

signature:
NLAlib.quadForm_transpose_mul_self.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] {m : Type u_2} [Fintype m] (A : Matrix m n ℝ)

signature: NLAlib.rademacherMeasure : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ
name: NLAlib.rademacherMeasure
doc:
The concrete Rademacher probability measure, assigning mass one half to each of
`1` and `-1`. This is exactly the law used by `IsRademacher`.
Atlas `hutchinson-unbiased`, `hutchinson-variance`.
atlas: scalar-laws-def

signature:
NLAlib.rademacher_hutchinson_moments.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {g : Ω → ℝ} (hg : AEMeasurable g μ) (hlaw : NLAlib.IsRademacher μ g) :
  MeasureTheory.MemLp g 2 μ ∧
    ∫ (ω : Ω), g ω ∂μ = 0 ∧
      ∫ (ω : Ω), g ω ^ 2 ∂μ = 1 ∧ MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => g ω ^ 4) μ ∧ ∫ (ω : Ω), g ω ^ 4 ∂μ = 1
name: NLAlib.rademacher_hutchinson_moments

signature:
NLAlib.rademacher_matrix_mgf_cgf_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
  (g : Ω → ℝ) (hMeas : Measurable g) (hLaw : NLAlib.IsRademacher μ g) (θ : ℝ) :
  NLAlib.LoewnerLE (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ * g ω) • A) ∂μ) (NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ ^ 2 / 2) • A ^ 2)) ∧
    NLAlib.LoewnerLE (NLAlib.matrixLog (∫ (ω : Ω), NLAlib.matrixExp ((θ * g ω) • A) ∂μ)) ((θ ^ 2 / 2) • A ^ 2)
name: NLAlib.rademacher_matrix_mgf_cgf_le
doc:
For a Rademacher `g` and Hermitian `A`, `𝔼 matrixExp (θ g A) ≼ matrixExp (θ²/2 • A²)` and its
logarithm is `≼ θ²/2 • A²`.

Tropp 2015, Lemma 4.6.3. Atlas: `matrix-gaussian-series`. Ported from the Prove2me mission *An
Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities, Ch 4*.

signature:
NLAlib.range_aeval_mul_le_blockKrylovSpace.{u_1, u_2} {n : Type u_1} {s : Type u_2} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

atlas: block-krylov-subspace

signature:
NLAlib.range_arnoldiMatrix.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (b : n → ℝ) (q : ℕ) :

signature:
NLAlib.range_mulVecLin_mul_eq_of_rank_eq {m n t : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) (Z : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ)

A matrix whose range is contained in `range A` and has the same rank as `A`
spans exactly that range. This is the deterministic exact-range step, not merely

[`saad11`], §5.1, Alg. 5.1.
atlas: subspace-iteration-def

signature:

(`frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, i.e.
`‖A − QQᵀA‖_F ≤ ‖A − QB‖_F` for every `B`, applied to `B = QᵀZ`), the untruncated analogue
of the argument for `Q⟦QᵀA⟧ₖ`. (Equivalently, `frobSq (A − Q(QᵀA)) ≤ frobSq (A − QY)` for
the truncated output, see `frobSq_sub_mul_transpose_mul_le_frobSq_sub_mul`.)
Conclusion: `E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²`.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error`.

signature:

  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {m : Type u_2} {q : Type u_3} [Fintype m] [Fintype q] [DecidableEq q]

  {V₁ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin k) ℝ} {V₂ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin r') ℝ} {S₁ : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ}
  {S₂ : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r') ℝ} (hA : A = U₁ * S₁ * V₁.transpose + U₂ * S₂ * V₂.transpose)
  (hU₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols U₂) (hV₁ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₁) (hV₂ : NLAlib.HasOrthonormalCols V₂)
  (hV : V₁.transpose * V₂ = 0) (hkt : k + 2 ≤ t) (Ω : Ωs → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin t) ℝ)
  (hΩ : MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω => Matrix.of.symm (Ω ω)) μ = NLAlib.gaussianMatrix n t) (Q : Ωs → Matrix m q ℝ)

  (hQr : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ωs) ∂μ, Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * (A * Ω ω)) = A * Ω ω) :
  ∫ (ω : Ωs), NLAlib.frobSq (A - Q ω * ((Q ω).transpose * A)) ∂μ ≤ (1 + ↑k / (↑t - ↑k - 1)) * NLAlib.frobSq S₂

doc:
**Randomized SVD with a Gaussian test matrix** (Chen–Persson, Theorem `thm:RSVD`, Algorithm
RSVD; HMT 2011, Thm 10.5, Frobenius case): if `Ω` is an `n × t` standard Gaussian matrix,
`t ≥ k + 2`, and `Q ω` has a.s. orthonormal columns with `range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then
`E‖A − QQᵀA‖_F² ≤ (1 + k/(t−k−1)) ‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F²` (`‖A − ⟦A⟧ₖ‖_F² = frobSq S₂` via the block SVD).
`rsvd_main` with its Gaussian hypotheses `hunit`, `hinv`, `hZi` discharged. The integrability
hypothesis `hXi` is also removed: when the error is not integrable its Bochner integral is `0`
and the (nonnegative) bound holds trivially. No measurability of `Q` is required.
Deviation: `n`, `k`, `r`, `r'`, `t` are `Fin` (the Gaussian law of `Ω` and the block lemmas of
`Gaussian/Conditioning.lean` live on `Fin`); the row type `m` and the column type `q` of `Q`
are arbitrary.
Atlas `rsvd-expected-error` (uses `gaussian-conditioning`, `pinv-frob-moment`,
`gaussian-full-rank-ae`, `hmt-9-1-frobenius`).

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_inv_self_mul_transpose_eq.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]

**Spectral norm of the inverse Gram matrix.** For every real matrix `A`,
`‖(A Aᵀ)⁻¹‖ = 1 / σ_min(Aᵀ)²`, i.e. `λ_max((A Aᵀ)⁻¹) = 1 / λ_min(A Aᵀ)`. When `A Aᵀ` is

`pinv-spectral-tail`, `inverse-wishart-spectral-moment` (helper). Generalised from
`Fin r × Fin k` to arbitrary finite index types. Ported from Prove2me solution
`GaussianMatrix.specNorm_inv_gram_eq`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_le_div_of_net.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (N : Finset (n → ℝ)) {ε M : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (hM0 : 0 ≤ M)
  (hN : ∀ (y : n → ℝ), y ⬝ᵥ y = 1 → ∃ x ∈ N, (x - y) ⬝ᵥ (x - y) ≤ ε ^ 2)
  (hM : ∀ x ∈ N, √(A.mulVec x ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x) ≤ M) : NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ M / (1 - ε)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_le_div_of_net
doc:
**Spectral norm from a net (operator form).** If `N` is an `ε`-net of the unit sphere
(`∀ y` unit, `∃ x ∈ N`, `‖x - y‖₂ ≤ ε`) with `0 ≤ ε < 1`, and `‖Ax‖₂ ≤ M` for every `x ∈ N`
(`M ≥ 0`), then `‖A‖₂ ≤ M/(1-ε)`. The net points need not be unit vectors. `hM0` is needed:
for an empty index type `N` may be empty and `M` negative.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.3 (i); Vershynin 2018, Ex 4.4.3; audit G1 C8. Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`
(deterministic half).
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_le_div_of_net_bilinear.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]
  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) (N : Finset (n → ℝ)) (N' : Finset (m → ℝ)) {ε M : ℝ} (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε)
  (hε1 : ε < 1 / 2) (hM0 : 0 ≤ M) (hN'unit : ∀ y ∈ N', y ⬝ᵥ y = 1)
  (hN : ∀ (x : n → ℝ), x ⬝ᵥ x = 1 → ∃ x₀ ∈ N, (x₀ - x) ⬝ᵥ (x₀ - x) ≤ ε ^ 2)
  (hN' : ∀ (y : m → ℝ), y ⬝ᵥ y = 1 → ∃ y₀ ∈ N', (y₀ - y) ⬝ᵥ (y₀ - y) ≤ ε ^ 2)
  (hM : ∀ x ∈ N, ∀ y ∈ N', y ⬝ᵥ A.mulVec x ≤ M) : NLAlib.specNorm A ≤ M / (1 - 2 * ε)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_le_div_of_net_bilinear
doc:
**Spectral norm from two nets (bilinear form).** If `N` and `N'` are `ε`-nets of the unit
spheres of `ℝⁿ` and `ℝᵐ`, the points of `N'` being unit vectors, `0 ≤ ε < 1/2`, and `yᵀ A x ≤ M` for all
`x ∈ N`, `y ∈ N'` (`M ≥ 0`), then `‖A‖₂ ≤ M/(1-2ε)`.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.4 (bilinear form); Vershynin 2018, Ex 4.4.3 (b); audit G1 C8.
Atlas `epsilon-net-norm` (deterministic half).
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

doc:
**Spectral norm of a symmetric matrix from a net (quadratic form).** If `B` is symmetric,
`N` is an `ε`-net of the unit sphere made of unit vectors, `0 ≤ ε < 1/2`, and
`|xᵀ B x| ≤ M` for every `x ∈ N`, then `‖B‖₂ ≤ M/(1-2ε)`.
Vershynin 2012, Lem 5.4; Vershynin 2018, Ex 4.4.3 (c); audit G1 C8. Atlas `epsilon-net-norm`
(deterministic half).
atlas: epsilon-net-norm

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_eq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) = if A.rank = 0 then 0 else 1 / NLAlib.singularValues A (A.rank - 1)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_eq
doc:
The complete spectral-norm formula for the general Moore–Penrose inverse:
zero at rank zero and the reciprocal of the smallest positive singular value
otherwise. Empty dimensions are covered by the rank-zero branch.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_eq_fintype.{u_1, u_2} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
  [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :
  NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) =
    if A.rank = 0 then 0
    else 1 / NLAlib.singularValues ((Matrix.reindex (Fintype.equivFin m) (Fintype.equivFin n)) A) (A.rank - 1)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_eq_fintype
doc:
The Moore–Penrose norm on general indices is zero at rank zero and the
reciprocal of the last positive singular value otherwise. Horn–Johnson §7.3;
atlas `pseudoinverse`. The list uses explicit `Fin(card)` normalization.
atlas: pseudoinverse

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_eq_inv_singularValues_last_positive {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ)
  (hr : 0 < A.rank) : NLAlib.specNorm (NLAlib.moorePenroseInverse A) = 1 / NLAlib.singularValues A (A.rank - 1)
name: NLAlib.specNorm_moorePenroseInverse_eq_inv_singularValues_last_positive
doc:
For positive rank, the spectral norm of the general inverse is the
reciprocal of the smallest positive singular value, at index `rank A - 1`.
This is the correct formula for rank-deficient matrices as well as full-rank
matrices. Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

signature:

  [DecidableEq n] (A : Matrix m n ℝ) :

doc:
The squared spectral norm of the general inverse equals the spectral
norm of the general inverse of the row Gram matrix, at every rank.
Horn–Johnson §7.3; atlas `pseudoinverse`.

`‖A†‖² = ‖(A Aᵀ)⁻¹‖` with `A† = pinvR A = Aᵀ (A Aᵀ)⁻¹` (`C*`-identity
`‖A†‖² = ‖(A†)ᵀ A†‖` and `(A†)ᵀ A† = (A Aᵀ)⁻¹`; both sides `0` when `A Aᵀ` is singular).

HMT 2011, proof of Prop A.3 / Prop 10.4. Atlas: `pseudoinverse`; helper for
`pinv-spectral-tail`. Generalised from `Fin r × Fin k` to arbitrary finite index types.
Ported from Prove2me solution `GaussianMatrix.specNorm_pinvR_sq`.
atlas: pseudoinverse

`specNorm_residual_sq_le_of_range_subset`, `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖ ≤ ‖Σ₂‖ + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖`

signature:
NLAlib.specNorm_residual_le_rpow.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m]

doc:
**Deterministic power-iteration bound** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.2, as printed):
`‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖ ≤ ‖(I − QQᵀ)(AAᵀ)^q A‖^{1/(2q+1)}` for any `Q` with orthonormal columns.
Deviation: no `Q = orth((AAᵀ)^q AΩ)` hypothesis (see `specNorm_residual_pow_le`).
Atlas `power-iteration-deterministic`.
atlas: power-iteration-deterministic

signature:

name: NLAlib.specNorm_residual_pow_le
doc:
**Deterministic power-iteration bound** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.2, power form): for `Q` with
orthonormal columns and `q ≥ 0`, `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖^{2q+1} ≤ ‖(I − QQᵀ)(AAᵀ)^q A‖`.
Deviation: the source takes `Q = orth((AAᵀ)^q AΩ)`; the inequality holds for every `Q` with
orthonormal columns, so that hypothesis is dropped. Atlas `power-iteration-deterministic`.
atlas: power-iteration-deterministic

name: NLAlib.specNorm_residual_sq_le_of_range_subset
doc:
**Deterministic range-finder bound, spectral form** (HMT 2011, Thm 9.1, spectral case): if
`A = U₁Σ₁V₁ᵀ + U₂Σ₂V₂ᵀ`, `Ω₁ = V₁ᵀΩ` has full row rank, `Ω₂ = V₂ᵀΩ`, `QᵀQ = I` and
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`, then `‖(I − QQᵀ)A‖² ≤ ‖Σ₂‖² + ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖²`.

Deviations from the printed statement: the hypotheses are those of the Frobenius form
`frobSq_residual_le_of_range_subset`, verbatim (block decomposition with `U₂ᵀU₂ = I`,
`V₁ᵀV₁ = I`, `V₂ᵀV₂ = I`, `V₁ᵀV₂ = 0`; no diagonality, no conditions on `U₁`, no completeness;
`Σ₁` need not be invertible); `P_Y` is `QQᵀ` for any orthonormal `Q` with
`range(AΩ) ⊆ range(Q)`; index types other than the rank `Fin k` are arbitrary `Fintype`s.
Atlas `hmt-9-1-spectral` (assumed → proved).
atlas: hmt-9-1-spectral

signature:
NLAlib.sub_mem_krylovSpace_iff_exists_sub_mulVec_eq.{u_1} {n : Type u_1} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n ℝ}
  (hA : IsUnit A) {c x₀ x : n → ℝ} {q : ℕ} :
  x - x₀ ∈ NLAlib.krylovSpace A (c - A.mulVec x₀) q ↔
    ∃ p, p.degree ≤ ↑q ∧ Polynomial.eval 0 p = 1 ∧ c - A.mulVec x = ((Polynomial.aeval A) p).mulVec (c - A.mulVec x₀)
name: NLAlib.sub_mem_krylovSpace_iff_exists_sub_mulVec_eq
doc:
**Residual-polynomial characterisation of `x₀ + K_q`.** For invertible `A`,
`x − x₀ ∈ K_q(A, r₀) ↔ ∃ p, deg p ≤ q ∧ p(0) = 1 ∧ c − A x = p(A) r₀`.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], §6.11; Trefethen–Bau (1997) [`tb97`], Lect. 35.
Deviation: the converse direction needs `A` injective (`IsUnit A`); the forward direction
(`exists_sub_mulVec_eq_aeval_mulVec_of_sub_mem_krylovSpace`) holds for every `A`.
atlas: residual-polynomial (partial)

name: NLAlib.sub_mem_krylovSpace_krylovGrade
doc:
**Finite termination.** If `A` is invertible and `A x⋆ = c`, then for every `x₀` the error
`x⋆ − x₀` lies in `K_ν(A, r₀)`, `r₀ = c − A x₀`, `ν = ν(A, r₀)`; so every Krylov method that
minimises over `x₀ + K_q` is exact at `q = ν`. The proof: `A` maps the invariant space `K_ν`
injectively, hence onto, itself, and `r₀ = A (x⋆ − x₀)` lies in it.
Source: Saad (2003) [`saad03`], Prop 6.3 and §6.1 (`A⁻¹ b ∈ K_ν(A, b)`).
Atlas: `krylov-grade` (partial: finite termination).
atlas: krylov-grade (partial)

doc:

`tan² ∠(u, x) = (‖u‖² ‖x‖² − ⟨u, x⟩²)/⟨u, x⟩²`. For a unit `u` this is
`‖(I − u uᵀ) x‖²/⟨u, x⟩²`. Junk value `0` when `⟨u, x⟩ = 0` (the angle is `π/2`).
Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1 (where `tan θ(u, x)` is used with `‖u‖ = 1`).
Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle` (belongs with principal angles in `NLAlib.Matrix`).

name: NLAlib.tanSqAngle_aeval_mulVec_le
doc:
**Eigenvector angle, polynomial form.** For real symmetric `A`, an index `i₁`, and any
polynomial `p` with `|p(λᵢ)| ≤ M` for every `i ≠ i₁`,
`tan² ∠(u_{i₁}, p(A) b) ≤ (M/p(λ_{i₁}))² tan² ∠(u_{i₁}, b)`. With `deg p < q`, `p(A) b ∈ K_q(A, b)`.
No hypothesis on `b` or `p(λ_{i₁})` is needed (both sides use the junk value `0` for a right
angle). Source: Saad (2011) [`saad11`], §6.6.1, proof of the angle bound (`i = 1`).
atlas: krylov-eigenvector-angle (partial)

Helper for `krylov-eigenvector-angle`.
